Name: Ab Scissors
How to: Lie on your back with the lower back pressed flat and both legs raised a few inches off the floor. Lower one leg toward the ground as the other rises, then switch in a steady scissoring rhythm.
Form check: Lower back stays pinned to the floor · Legs stay long · Raise the legs higher if the back arches

Name: Ab Wheel (Eccentric)
How to: Roll out from the knees through a longer range than you can return from, taking three to five seconds on the way out. Lower to the floor at the end and reset for the next rep.
Form check: Three to five seconds out · Go past your normal range · Reset from the floor each rep

Name: Ab Wheel (Kneeling)
How to: Kneel with the wheel under your shoulders and grip the handles. Tuck the pelvis, then roll out as far as you can keep a flat back and pull yourself back with the abs.
Form check: Tuck the pelvis before rolling · Flat back, no arching · Pull back with the abs not the arms

Name: Ab Wheel (Standing)
How to: Start standing with the wheel on the floor in front of your feet. Roll out to full extension without letting the knees touch, then pull yourself all the way back to standing.
Form check: Knees never touch the floor · Flat back the whole way · Use a wall as a stop while learning

Name: Aerobics
How to: Follow a continuous routine of rhythmic, low impact movements that keeps the heart rate up for the whole session. Keep moving between moves rather than stopping so the effort stays steady.
Form check: Keep moving between moves · Land softly through the whole foot · Breathe in rhythm with the pace

Name: Air Bike
How to: Lie on your back with hands lightly beside your head and lift your shoulders off the floor. Bring one knee toward your chest as you rotate the opposite elbow to meet it. Switch sides in a pedaling motion, extending the free leg out straight.
Form check: Twist elbow to opposite knee · Don't yank the neck · Fully straighten the free leg

Name: Arch Hang
How to: Hang from the bar and pull the shoulder blades down, then arch the chest toward the bar while looking up. Hold briefly and return to a hollow hang.
Form check: Chest up toward the bar · Shoulders stay pulled down · Alternate hollow and arch

Name: Arnold Press (Dumbbell)
How to: Start with the dumbbells in front of the shoulders, palms facing you. Press overhead while rotating the palms to face forward, then reverse the rotation on the way down.
Form check: Rotate smoothly through the press · keep the core braced · don't flare or bounce at the bottom · control the full range

Name: Around The World
How to: Lie on a bench holding a light dumbbell in each hand at your hips, palms up. Sweep both arms out and around in a wide arc until they meet above your head, then trace the same path back.
Form check: Keep a soft bend in the elbows · Go light, the leverage is long · Trace the same arc on the way back

Name: Assisted Pistol Squats
How to: Hold a doorframe or strap for light assistance and lower on one leg with the other held out in front. Use the hands only as much as needed to reach the bottom.
Form check: Free leg stays off the floor · Least assistance that works · Heel stays down

Name: Back Extension (Hyperextension)
How to: Set the pad just below your hip bones and hook your heels under the rollers. Fold at the hips until your torso hangs down, then raise until your body forms a straight line and stop there.
Form check: Pad below the hip bones · Stop level, do not arch past straight · Bend at the hips not the spine

Name: Back Extension (Machine)
How to: Sit in the machine with the pad across your upper back and your feet planted. Press back by extending the spine and hips until your torso is upright, then return under control without letting the weight slam.
Form check: Set the pad across the upper back · Stop at upright · Return slowly, do not let the stack drop

Name: Back Extension (Weighted Hyperextension)
How to: Hold a plate against your chest or behind your head on the hyperextension bench. Fold at the hips and raise back to a straight line, keeping the same range you use unloaded.
Form check: Hold the plate close to the chest · Stop level, do not arch · Add load only once the range is clean

Name: Ball Slams
How to: Stand with the slam ball at your feet and lift it overhead with straight arms. Drive it into the floor as hard as you can, hinging at the hips, then squat to pick it up and repeat.
Form check: Hinge as you slam, do not fold the back · Follow the ball down · Squat to pick it up, do not round over

Name: Band Pullaparts
How to: Hold a band with both hands, arms extended straight out in front at shoulder height. Keeping your elbows locked, pull the band apart by driving your hands out to your sides until it meets your chest. Return slowly to the front.
Form check: Keep elbows locked, pull to your chest · Stay tall, don't shrug up

Name: Bar Pullover
How to: Pull hard until the bar reaches the waist, then lean the shoulders forward and rotate over the bar into a straight arm support.
Form check: Pull to the waist before rotating · Lean the shoulders over early · Keep the bar close to the body

Name: Battle Ropes
How to: Anchor a heavy rope at its center and hold one end in each hand with arms at your sides. Drop into a slight athletic quarter-squat and brace your core. Rapidly raise and lower each arm to drive alternating waves down the rope, keeping them fast and continuous.
Form check: Sit into a quarter-squat · Drive fast, tall waves · Keep both arms moving evenly

Name: Behind the Back Bicep Wrist Curl (Barbell)
How to: Stand upright holding a barbell behind your back with an overhand grip and let it hang at your fingertips. Curl the bar up by closing the fingers and flexing the wrists, then lower it back to the fingertips.
Form check: Let the bar roll to the fingertips · Move only the wrists · Keep the elbows still against your sides

Name: Bench Dip
How to: Sit on a bench with the hands beside the hips and the feet on the floor in front of you. Slide off the edge and lower until the elbows bend to a right angle, then press back up.
Form check: Elbows point back, not out · Keep the hips close to the bench · Stop at ninety degrees

Name: Bench Press (Barbell)
How to: Lie on a flat bench and take a grip that puts the forearms vertical at the bottom. Unrack and hold the bar over the chest with locked arms. Lower under control until it touches mid-chest, pause, then press back up and squeeze the chest at the top.
Form check: Forearms roughly vertical at the bottom · lower about twice as slowly as you press · drive from the chest · keep the wrists stacked over the elbows

Name: Bench Press (Cable)
How to: Lie on a bench set between two low cable pulleys and take a handle in each hand at chest height. Press both handles up and slightly together until the arms lock, then lower to a stretch at chest level.
Form check: Set the pulleys level with your chest · Press up and slightly in · Keep tension on the cables at the bottom

Name: Bench Press (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie back on a flat bench with a dumbbell in each hand at chest height, palms facing forward. Press both dumbbells up until the arms are straight, then lower until your elbows sit just below the bench line.
Form check: Wrists stacked over the elbows · Lower to a deep but pain free stretch · Keep the shoulder blades pinned back

Name: Bench Press (Smith Machine)
How to: Set the seat so the handles line up with the mid-chest. Press the handles forward until the arms are extended, then return under control to a stretch.
Form check: Adjust the seat so handles meet the mid-chest · keep the back against the pad · don't let the shoulders roll forward · control the return, don't let it slam

Name: Bench Press - Close Grip (Barbell)
How to: Lie back on a flat bench and grip the bar at about shoulder width. Unrack it and hold it over your chest with arms locked. Lower the bar slowly to your lower chest with elbows tucked close to your sides, then press it back up until your arms lock out.
Form check: Grip about shoulder width · Tuck elbows to your sides · Push through your triceps

Name: Bench Press - Wide Grip (Barbell)
How to: Lie on a flat bench with feet planted. Take a wide, overhand grip a few inches outside shoulder width and unrack the bar over your chest. Lower it to mid-chest with elbows flared out, then press back up to full lockout.
Form check: Grip a hand-width outside shoulders · Pin your shoulder blades back · Flare your elbows out · Lower to mid-chest

Name: Bent Over Row (Band)
How to: Stand on the middle of the band and hinge forward with a flat back, holding one end in each hand. Pull the handles to your waist by driving the elbows back, then straighten the arms under control.
Form check: Hinge until the torso is near parallel · Pull to the waist not the chest · Squeeze the shoulder blades together

Name: Bent Over Row (Barbell)
How to: Hinge forward with a flat back until your torso is close to parallel and let the barbell hang at arms length. Row the bar to your lower ribs by pulling the elbows back, then lower it under control.
Form check: Flat back the whole set · Pull to the lower ribs · Do not jerk the torso upright to move the bar

Name: Bent Over Row (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward at the waist, knees slightly bent, back flat until your torso is almost parallel to the floor. Let the dumbbells hang at arm's length. Row them up to your sides, squeezing your back, then lower under control.
Form check: Hinge to near parallel, back flat · Row the bells up to your sides

Name: Bicep Curl (Barbell)
How to: Stand tall holding the bar with an underhand shoulder-width grip and elbows pinned to the sides. Curl to the shoulders by contracting the biceps, then lower under control.
Form check: Elbows stay pinned at the sides · no swinging or hip drive · squeeze at the top · lower slowly to a full stretch

Name: Bicep Curl (Cable)
How to: Stand facing a low pulley with a straight bar or handle and your elbows tucked at your sides. Curl the handle up to shoulder height, then lower it slowly against the constant pull of the cable.
Form check: Elbows pinned at your sides · No swinging back · Fight the cable on the way down

Name: Bicep Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand upright with a dumbbell in each hand, arms at your sides and palms facing your thighs. Curl one dumbbell up while rotating your palm to face up, keeping the upper arm still. Lower it and repeat with the other arm.
Form check: Rotate palm up as you lift · Keep upper arms fixed · Alternate arms each rep

Name: Bicep Curl (Machine)
How to: Sit with your upper arms flat on the pad and grip the handles with your arms nearly straight. Curl the handles up toward your shoulders, then lower until the arms are almost straight again.
Form check: Upper arms flat on the pad throughout · Stop just short of locking out · Lower slower than you lift

Name: Bicep Curl (Suspension)
How to: Hold the handles with palms up and walk your feet forward so your body leans back. Curl your body up by bending only at the elbows, keeping the upper arms high and still, then lower under control.
Form check: Upper arms stay up and fixed · Body stays in one straight line · Walk the feet back to make it easier

Name: Bicycle Crunch
How to: Lie on your back with hands lightly beside your head and lift your shoulders off the floor. Bring one knee toward your chest as you rotate the opposite elbow to meet it. Switch sides in a pedaling motion, extending the free leg out straight.
Form check: Twist elbow to opposite knee · Don't yank the neck · Fully straighten the free leg

Name: Bicycle Crunch Raised Legs
How to: Lie on your back with both legs raised and bent at ninety degrees and your hands light beside your head. Bring one elbow toward the opposite knee while the other leg extends, then switch sides.
Form check: Do not pull on the neck · Rotate through the ribs not the elbows · Keep the lower back flat

Name: Bird Dog
How to: Start on hands and knees with a flat back. Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back until both are level with your torso, hold briefly, then return and switch sides.
Form check: Hips stay square to the floor · Reach long rather than lifting high · Keep the back flat, no sagging

Name: Box Jump
How to: Stand a short step from the box with your feet hip width. Dip and swing the arms, jump up and land softly on the box with both feet flat and knees bent, then step down one foot at a time.
Form check: Land soft with the whole foot on the box · Step down, do not jump down · Pick a height you can land quietly

Name: Box Squat (Barbell)
How to: Set a flat bench or box behind you and unrack a barbell across your upper back. Stand just in front of the bench with feet shoulder-width. Push your hips back and squat down until you lightly touch the bench, then drive through your heels to stand.
Form check: Push the hips back to the bench · Touch light, don't crash down · Drive up off the bench

Name: Boxing
How to: Work rounds on a bag or on pads, throwing combinations while keeping your hands up and your feet moving. Keep the pace continuous so the round stays a cardio effort rather than a set of singles.
Form check: Hands back to the chin after every punch · Turn the hips into the shot · Keep moving between combinations

Name: Bulgarian Split Squat
How to: Stand a stride in front of a bench and rest the top of the rear foot on it. Lower until the front thigh is parallel to the floor, then drive back up through the front heel.
Form check: Front shin near vertical · Rear foot on the bench · Drive through the front heel

Name: Burpee
How to: From standing, drop your hands to the floor and shoot your feet back into a push up position, then lower your chest to the ground. Jump the feet back under you and stand up into a jump with the hands overhead.
Form check: Chest touches the floor at the bottom · Keep the hips from sagging in the plank · Finish with a full jump

Name: Burpee Over the Bar
How to: Perform a burpee beside a loaded barbell, dropping your chest to the floor. Stand and jump laterally over the bar with both feet, then turn and repeat facing the other way.
Form check: Chest to the floor each rep · Clear the bar with both feet · Land soft with bent knees

Name: Butterfly (Pec Deck)
How to: Sit in the pec deck with your back flat against the pad and your forearms or hands on the pads at chest height. Squeeze the pads together in front of your chest, then let them open slowly to a stretch.
Form check: Back stays flat on the pad · Squeeze the chest, not the hands · Open slowly to a stretch, do not bounce

Name: Cable Core Palloff Press
How to: Stand side on to a cable set at chest height and hold the handle at your sternum with both hands. Press it straight out in front of you and resist the pull that wants to twist you, then bring it back.
Form check: Resist the twist, do not rotate · Stay square to the front · Brace the abs before pressing out

Name: Cable Crunch
How to: Kneel below a high pulley holding the rope by the head. Crunch down by flexing the spine and contracting the abs, bringing the elbows toward the thighs, then return under control.
Form check: Round the spine, flex, don't just hip-fold · keep the hips fixed · drive with the abs, not the arms · don't go so heavy the lower back takes over

Name: Cable Fly Crossovers
How to: Stand between two high pulleys with a handle in each hand and one foot forward. Sweep the handles down and across until they cross in front of your hips, then open the arms back to a chest stretch.
Form check: Soft bend in the elbows throughout · Cross the hands at the bottom · Lead with the elbows not the hands

Name: Cable Pull Through
How to: Face away from a low pulley with the rope passed between your legs and take a step forward. Hinge back until you feel the hamstrings stretch, then drive the hips forward to stand tall and squeeze the glutes.
Form check: Drive with the hips, do not pull with the arms · Flat back through the hinge · Finish standing tall, no lean back

Name: Cable Twist (Down to up)
How to: Set the cable low and stand side on holding the handle with both hands near your outside hip. Rotate up and across your body to shoulder height, turning through the torso and pivoting the back foot.
Form check: Turn through the ribs, not just the arms · Pivot the back foot · Keep the arms fairly straight

Name: Cable Twist (Up to down)
How to: Set the cable high and stand side on holding the handle with both hands above one shoulder. Pull down and across your body toward the opposite hip, rotating the torso and pivoting the back foot.
Form check: Rotate the torso, do not just pull the arms · Pivot the back foot · Control the return, no snapping back

Name: Calf Extension (Machine)
How to: Position the balls of your feet on the platform with the pad on your shoulders or thighs. Press up onto your toes as high as you can, then lower the heels below the platform for a full stretch.
Form check: Balls of the feet on the edge · Full stretch at the bottom · Pause at the top rather than bouncing

Name: Calf Press (Machine)
How to: Sit in the leg press and place just the balls of your feet on the lower edge of the platform, heels off. Release the safety bars and straighten your legs. Press the platform away by extending your ankles and squeezing the calves, then let your toes come back.
Form check: Balls of feet on the platform edge · Full stretch down, press onto the toes

Name: Chest Dip
How to: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms and a tall chest. Lower until the shoulders drop to elbow height, then press back up to a locked out top position.
Form check: Lower until shoulders reach elbow height · Elbows close to the body · Lock out at the top

Name: Chest Dip (Assisted)
How to: Kneel on the assist pad or loop a band under your knees on the parallel bars and lean your chest forward. Lower until your shoulders reach elbow height, then press back to straight arms.
Form check: Lean the chest forward the whole rep · Lower to shoulders at elbow height · Use only as much assistance as you need

Name: Chest Dip (Eccentric)
How to: Jump or step to the top of the parallel bars with straight arms. Lower yourself as slowly as you can until the shoulders reach elbow height, then step off and reset.
Form check: Three to five seconds down · Elbows stay close to the body · Step off and reset each rep

Name: Chest Dip (Weighted)
How to: Attach additional load with a dip belt or vest. Lower through a controlled full range, then press to locked arms without losing shoulder position.
Form check: Record added load only · Full depth · Elbows track back · Full lockout
Equipment: Dip bars; weight belt or vest

Name: Chest Fly (Band)
How to: Anchor the band behind you at chest height and hold one end in each hand with the arms out wide. Bring your hands together in front of your chest with a soft elbow bend, then open slowly back to a stretch.
Form check: Soft bend in the elbows throughout · Bring the hands together in front of the chest · Step forward for more tension

Name: Chest Fly (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand above your chest with a soft elbow bend. Open the arms out in a wide arc until you feel a chest stretch, then bring them back together over your chest.
Form check: Keep the elbow angle fixed · Open only as far as is comfortable · Go lighter than you would for a press

Name: Chest Fly (Machine)
How to: Sit with your back flat against the pad and grip the handles with your arms out to the sides and elbows slightly bent. Bring the handles together in front of your chest, then open slowly back to a stretch.
Form check: Back flat on the pad · Elbows stay at the same angle · Pause and squeeze at the front

Name: Chest Fly (Suspension)
How to: Hold a handle in each hand and lean forward with your body straight and arms in front of your chest. Open the arms out to the sides as you lower, then squeeze them back together to press yourself upright.
Form check: Body stays in one straight line · Open only as wide as you can control · Walk the feet back to make it easier

Name: Chest Press (Band)
How to: Anchor the band behind you at chest height and hold an end in each hand beside your chest. Press both hands forward until your arms are straight, then return slowly against the band.
Form check: Anchor the band level with the chest · Press straight forward · Resist the band on the way back

Name: Chest Press (Machine)
How to: Sit with your back flat on the pad and the handles level with the middle of your chest. Press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight, then return until you feel a stretch across the chest.
Form check: Set the seat so the handles sit at mid chest · Stop just short of locking out · Keep the shoulder blades pinned back

Name: Chest Supported Incline Row (Dumbbell)
How to: Set an incline bench and lie chest-down against it with a dumbbell in each hand, neutral grip, arms hanging straight. Squeeze your shoulder blades and row both dumbbells up by driving your elbows back. Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Form check: Keep your chest on the bench · squeeze your shoulder blades first · Drive the elbows back and up

Name: Chest Supported Reverse Fly (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie chest down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand hanging below you. Raise the arms out to the sides until they are level with your shoulders, then lower them under control.
Form check: Chest stays on the bench · Lead with the elbows · Stop level with the shoulders, no higher

Name: Chest Supported Y Raise (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie chest down on an incline bench with light dumbbells hanging below you and thumbs pointing up. Raise the arms overhead in a Y shape until they line up with your torso, then lower slowly.
Form check: Thumbs point up throughout · Go light, this is a small muscle · Raise into a Y, not straight out to the sides

Name: Chin Up
How to: Hang from the bar with an underhand grip about shoulder width and your shoulder blades pulled down. Pull until your chin clears the bar, then lower all the way to straight arms.
Form check: Underhand grip, hands about shoulder width · Chin clears the bar · Lower to fully straight arms

Name: Chin Up (Assisted)
How to: Set the assist machine or loop a band under your knee and take an underhand grip on the bar. Pull until your chin clears the bar, then lower under control to straight arms.
Form check: Use the least assistance you can manage · Chin clears the bar · Still lower to straight arms every rep

Name: Chin Up (One Arm)
How to: Hang from one hand with a supinated grip and pull until the chin clears the bar. Keep the body from twisting and lower all the way down.
Form check: Chin fully over the bar · Resist the twist · Full straight arm at the bottom

Name: Chin Up (One Arm, Half Range)
How to: Grip the bar with one hand in a supinated grip and pull through the top half of the range only. Lower under control and rest before the next rep.
Form check: Work the top half of the range · Supinated grip · Even work on both arms

Name: Chin Up (One Arm, Towel Assisted)
How to: Hang a towel over the bar next to your working hand. Pull with one arm while the free hand grips the towel low and gives only light help.
Form check: Grip the towel as low as you can · Working arm does the work · Even sets on both sides

Name: Chin Up (Weighted)
How to: Add load with a dip belt or a weight vest and hang from the bar with an underhand grip. Pull until your chin clears the bar, then lower to straight arms without letting the weight swing.
Form check: Record the added load only · Keep the body still, no swinging · Full range before you add more weight
Equipment: Pull-up bar; weight belt or vest

Name: Clamshell
How to: Lie on your side with your knees bent and stacked and your heels in line with your spine. Keeping the feet together, open the top knee as far as you can without rolling the hips back, then close slowly.
Form check: Hips stay stacked, do not roll back · Feet stay together · Open only as far as the hips stay still

Name: Clap Push Ups
How to: Set up in a push up position and lower your chest to just above the floor. Drive up hard enough to leave the ground, clap your hands, then land with soft elbows and absorb straight into the next rep.
Form check: Push hard enough to clear the floor · Land with bent elbows to absorb · Keep the body in one line throughout

Name: Clean
How to: Set up over a barbell with an overhand grip just outside your legs, hips down, back flat and chest up. Drive through the floor and extend your hips explosively, pulling the bar up your body. Shrug and drop under it to catch the bar racked on your shoulders.
Form check: Flat back off the floor · Bar brushes your thighs · Explode through the hips · Drop under to catch

Name: Clean and Jerk
How to: Clean the bar to the shoulders, then dip slightly and drive it overhead with the legs, splitting or squatting under to catch it locked out. Stand to finish.
Form check: Full hip extension on both the clean and the jerk · drive the jerk with the legs, not the arms · punch under a locked-out bar · recover with control, feet in line

Name: Clean and Press
How to: Set up over a barbell with a overhand grip slightly wider than shoulder width, hips down and back flat. Explosively extend your hips to clean the bar to your shoulders. Brace your core and press the bar overhead until your arms lock out, then lower it back to your shoulders.
Form check: Explode hips to clean · Catch in the front rack · Brace before pressing · Lock out overhead

Name: Clean Pull
How to: Set up over a barbell with an overhand or hook grip just outside your legs, hips down, back flat and chest up. Push through the floor to lift the bar past your knees, then extend your hips, knees and ankles explosively. Shrug tall and let the bar rise without catching it.
Form check: Keep the bar close · Full extend the hips, knees and ankles · No early arm pull

Name: Climbing
How to: Work up a climbing wall or route at a pace that keeps you moving continuously. Push through the legs to move upward and keep the arms relatively straight so the legs carry the work.
Form check: Drive with the legs, not the arms · Keep the hips close to the wall · Move steadily rather than in bursts

Name: Concentration Curl
How to: Sit on a bench with your legs apart and brace the back of your upper arm against the inside of your thigh. Curl the dumbbell up to your shoulder, squeeze, then lower until the arm is straight.
Form check: Upper arm braced on the thigh · No swinging the shoulder · Lower all the way to a straight arm

Name: Cross Body Hammer Curl
How to: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand and palms facing in. Without rotating your wrist, curl one dumbbell up and across your body toward the opposite shoulder. Lower it back to your side and repeat with the other arm.
Form check: Curl across to the opposite shoulder · Neutral grip, no wrist twist

Name: Crunch
How to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and your hands light beside your head. Curl the shoulders and upper back off the floor by shortening the abs, then lower back down under control.
Form check: Curl the spine, do not just lift the neck · Lower back stays on the floor · Hands rest light, no pulling

Name: Crunch (Machine)
How to: Sit in the ab machine with the pad across your chest and your feet hooked in place. Crunch forward by rounding the spine and contracting the abs, then return slowly against the weight.
Form check: Round the spine, do not just hip fold · Drive with the abs not the arms · Return slowly, no stack slam

Name: Crunch (Weighted)
How to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and hold a plate or dumbbell against your chest or overhead. Curl the shoulders off the floor, pause at the top, then lower under control.
Form check: Hold the weight close and still · Curl the spine, not the neck · Lower slowly rather than dropping back

Name: Curtsy Lunge (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand holding dumbbells at your sides and step one leg back and across behind the other, like a curtsy. Lower until the front thigh is near parallel, then push through the front heel to stand.
Form check: Step back and across, not straight back · Front knee tracks over the foot · Keep the chest tall and hips square

Name: Cycling
How to: Ride at a steady effort you can hold for the whole session, adjusting resistance or terrain to keep the heart rate in range. Keep the pedal stroke smooth rather than mashing at the top.
Form check: Set the saddle so the knee stays slightly bent at the bottom · Smooth circular pedal stroke · Hold a steady cadence

Name: Dead Bug
How to: Lie on your back with arms reaching toward the ceiling and knees bent over your hips at 90 degrees. Press your lower back flat into the floor. Slowly lower one arm overhead and the opposite leg toward the floor, then return and switch sides.
Form check: Pin lower back to floor · Lower opposite arm and leg

Name: Dead Hang
How to: Grip the bar with both hands about shoulder width and let your body hang with the arms straight. Keep the shoulders active by pulling them slightly down away from the ears and hold for time.
Form check: Arms straight, shoulders pulled down · Breathe steadily rather than holding your breath · Drop off before the grip fails

Name: Deadlift (Band)
How to: Stand on the middle of the band with feet hip width and hold one end in each hand. Hinge down with a flat back until you feel the hamstrings load, then stand tall by driving the hips forward.
Form check: Flat back from start to finish · Push the floor away with the legs · Finish standing tall, do not lean back

Name: Deadlift (Barbell)
How to: Set the bar over the mid-foot, hip-width stance, and grip just outside the knees. Take the slack out, flatten the back and brace, then push the floor away and stand tall, dragging the bar up the legs to a locked-out finish.
Form check: Bar over the mid-foot, shins near the bar · flat back, chest up, lats tight · push the floor away rather than yanking · lock the hips and knees together at the top

Name: Deadlift (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with your feet hip width. Hinge at the hips and lower the weights along the front of your legs, then drive the hips forward to stand tall.
Form check: Keep the dumbbells close to the legs · Flat back throughout · Push the hips back rather than squatting down

Name: Deadlift (Smith Machine)
How to: Set the bar low in the Smith machine and stand with it over the middle of your feet. Hinge down and grip the bar, then drive through the floor to stand tall, keeping the bar path locked in the rails.
Form check: Set the bar over mid foot · Flat back, chest up · The rails fix the path so drive straight up

Name: Deadlift (Trap bar)
How to: Stand in the center of a loaded trap bar and grip both handles. Lower your hips, lift your chest and look forward with a flat back. Push your feet through the floor to stand tall, driving with your legs, then hinge back down under control.
Form check: Stand centered in the bar · Push the floor away with your legs · Drive the knees, not just hips

Name: Deadlift High Pull
How to: Deadlift the bar from the floor and, as it passes the thighs, extend hard and pull it up to chest height with the elbows driving high and outside. Reverse the path and return the bar to the floor.
Form check: Extend the hips before the arms pull · Elbows finish high and wide · Lower the bar, do not drop it

Name: Decline Bench Press (Barbell)
How to: On a decline bench with feet secured, unrack and hold the bar over the lower chest. Lower under control to the lower chest, then press back up and lock out.
Form check: Bar tracks to the lower chest · keep the shoulder blades squeezed · control down, drive up · keep the wrists stacked over the elbows

Name: Decline Bench Press (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie on a decline bench with your legs hooked and a dumbbell in each hand at chest height. Press both dumbbells up until the arms are straight, then lower to a stretch at the lower chest.
Form check: Hook the legs in before you start · Lower to the lower chest · Have a spotter or use a manageable weight

Name: Decline Bench Press (Machine)
How to: Set the seat so the handles line up with the mid-chest. Press the handles forward until the arms are extended, then return under control to a stretch.
Form check: Adjust the seat so handles meet the mid-chest · keep the back against the pad · don't let the shoulders roll forward · control the return, don't let it slam

Name: Decline Bench Press (Smith Machine)
How to: Set a decline bench in a Smith machine and lie back so the bar sits over your lower chest. Take a overhand grip wider than shoulder width and unlock the bar. Lower it under control to your lower chest, then press it straight up and lock out.
Form check: Grip wider than shoulders · Lower to your lower chest

Name: Decline Chest Fly (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie on a decline bench holding dumbbells above your chest with a soft elbow bend. Open the arms wide in an arc until you feel the stretch, then bring them back together over the lower chest.
Form check: Keep the elbow angle fixed · Open only as far as is comfortable · Use a lighter weight than for pressing

Name: Decline Crunch
How to: Hook your legs at the top of a decline bench and lie back with your hands beside your head, elbows in. Press your lower back into the bench and curl your shoulders up toward your hips by flexing your abs. Squeeze, then lower under control.
Form check: Curl ribs toward your hips · Hands off the neck, elbows in · No swinging off the bench

Name: Decline Crunch (Weighted)
How to: Hook your legs at the top of a decline bench and hold a plate against your chest. Curl your torso up by rounding the spine, then lower under control without letting your back slam down.
Form check: Round the spine rather than hip folding · Hold the plate close · Lower slowly, do not drop back

Name: Decline Push Up
How to: Place the feet on a box or bench with the hands on the floor. Lower the chest to the floor and press back up while keeping the hips from sagging.
Form check: Higher feet means more load · No sagging hips · Chest to the floor

Name: Diamond Push Up
How to: Place the hands together under the chest so the thumbs and index fingers form a triangle. Lower with the elbows tucked and press back up.
Form check: Hands together under the chest · Elbows stay tucked · Stop if the wrists complain

Name: Downward Dog
How to: From hands and knees, tuck the toes and lift the hips up and back so your body makes an inverted V. Press the chest toward the thighs and let the heels sink toward the floor, then breathe and hold.
Form check: Hips high, chest toward the thighs · Bend the knees if the back rounds · Heels sink, they do not have to touch

Name: Drag Curl
How to: Hold a barbell with a palms-up grip and elbows drawn back behind your torso. Curl the bar up while dragging it straight along your body, driving your elbows back so the bar stays close. Lower it down along the same path.
Form check: Drag the bar up your torso · Drive your elbows back · Stop at your lower chest

Name: Dragon Flag
How to: Lie on a bench and grip behind your head. Drive your legs up and lift your whole body so only the shoulders stay on the bench, then lower the straight body slowly without letting the hips bend.
Form check: Only the shoulders stay on the bench · Body stays in one rigid line · Lower as slowly as you can control

Name: Dragonfly
How to: Lie on a bench holding behind your head and raise your body until it is nearly vertical on your shoulders. Lower it as one straight line under control until it hovers above the bench, then drive back up.
Form check: Hips do not pike on the way down · Shoulders stay planted · Shorten the lever by bending the knees to scale it

Name: Dumbbell Row
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and hinge forward at the hips with your knees slightly bent and back flat. Let the dumbbells hang at arm's length. Pull the dumbbells toward your torso by driving your elbows back, squeeze your upper back, then lower under control.
Form check: Hinge at the hips with a neutral back · Keep the torso still · Drive the elbows back toward the ribs · Lower under control to a full stretch

Name: Dumbbell Snatch
How to: Set a dumbbell on the floor between your feet and hinge down to grip it. Drive hard through the legs and hips to pull it up close to your body, then punch the hand through to lock it out overhead.
Form check: Drive with the hips, do not curl it up · Keep the dumbbell close to the body · Finish with the arm locked and the ribs down

Name: Dumbbell Squeeze Press
How to: Lie on a bench holding two dumbbells pressed hard together over your chest, palms facing each other. Keeping them squeezed together, lower to the chest and press back up while the pressure never lets off.
Form check: Squeeze the dumbbells together the whole set · Elbows stay close to the body · Use a weight you can keep pinned together

Name: Dumbbell Step Up
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and place one whole foot on a box at about knee height. Drive through that heel to stand up on the box, then lower back down under control with the same leg.
Form check: Whole foot on the box · Drive through the top heel, do not push off the back foot · Lower slowly rather than dropping

Name: Elbow to Knee
How to: Lie on your back and cross one ankle over the opposite bent knee, hands behind your head. Flex your spine and rotate to bring the opposite elbow toward the crossed knee until your obliques squeeze. Lower under control, then switch legs and sides.
Form check: Bring elbow to the crossed knee · Rotate the torso, not the neck

Name: Elliptical Trainer
How to: Step onto the pedals and take hold of the moving handles. Push down and around through the balls of your feet, driving each pedal through a smooth oval stride. Keep an upright posture and let your legs power the motion.
Form check: Drive the balls of your feet around the oval · Stand tall, don't lean on the handles

Name: EZ Bar Biceps Curl
How to: Stand tall holding an EZ bar at the wide outer handles with palms facing forward and elbows close to your torso. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders by flexing the biceps, then lower it slowly back to a full stretch.
Form check: Grip the wide outer handles · Keep elbows close to your torso

Name: Face Pull
How to: Set a rope on a high pulley and grab both ends with palms facing in. Pull the rope toward your face, separating your hands and flaring your elbows out until your hands reach your ears. Keep your upper arms parallel to the floor and lower under control.
Form check: Pull the rope to your forehead · Flare your elbows up and out · Split your hands at the finish

Name: Farmers Walk
How to: Pick up a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in each hand with a flat back and stand tall. Walk with short quick steps for the set distance or time, keeping the shoulders back and the ribs down.
Form check: Stand tall, shoulders back · Short quick steps · Set the weights down with a hinge, do not drop them

Name: Fire Hydrants
How to: Start on hands and knees with a flat back. Keeping the knee bent at ninety degrees, lift one leg out to the side as high as you can without tipping the hips, then lower it under control.
Form check: Hips stay level, do not tip over · Knee stays bent throughout · Lift only as far as the hips stay square

Name: Floor Press (Barbell)
How to: Lie on the floor under a barbell with your knees bent and unrack it over your chest. Lower until the backs of your upper arms touch the floor, pause, then press back to straight arms.
Form check: Pause when the arms touch the floor · Elbows tucked around forty five degrees · Press straight up, no bouncing off the floor

Name: Floor Press (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie on the floor with a dumbbell in each hand at chest height and knees bent. Press the dumbbells up until the arms are straight, then lower until the upper arms rest on the floor and pause.
Form check: Pause with the upper arms on the floor · Keep the elbows tucked in · Do not bounce the arms off the ground

Name: Floor Triceps Dip
How to: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and your hands beside your hips, fingers pointing forward. Press through the palms to lift your hips off the floor, then bend the elbows to lower and press back up.
Form check: Fingers point forward · Bend the elbows straight back, not out · Keep the hips close to the hands

Name: Flutter Kicks
How to: Lie facedown on a bench with your hips at the edge and hold the front for support. Straighten your legs so your toes hang off the floor. Squeeze your glutes to lift both legs, then alternate kicking each leg up and down in small, quick pulses without touching the floor.
Form check: Lift from the glutes, not the low back · Keep both legs straight and pulsing

Name: Frog Jumps
How to: Squat down low with your hands between your feet. Jump forward and up as far as you can, land softly in the same low squat, then reset and repeat.
Form check: Land softly straight back into the squat · Use the arms to drive the jump · Keep the chest up on landing

Name: Frog Pumps (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie on your back with the soles of your feet together and knees dropped out to the sides, holding a dumbbell on your hips. Drive the hips up by squeezing the glutes, then lower almost to the floor.
Form check: Soles together, knees stay out wide · Squeeze the glutes at the top · Short quick reps, do not rest at the bottom

Name: Front Lever Hold
How to: Hang from the bar and pull your shoulders down and back, then raise your body until it is horizontal and facing up. Hold that straight line for time without letting the hips drop.
Form check: Body stays horizontal and straight · Shoulders pulled down, arms straight · Tuck the knees to scale it down

Name: Front Lever Hold (Tuck)
How to: Hang from a bar and pull the knees to the chest while rotating back so the back faces the floor and the shins point forward. Hold with the arms straight.
Form check: Back parallel to the floor · Knees tight to the chest · Arms stay locked

Name: Front Lever Raise
How to: From a hang, pull your shoulders down and lift your straight body up to horizontal, then lower it back to the hang under control. Keep the arms straight for the whole movement.
Form check: Arms stay straight throughout · Lower under control, do not drop · Tuck or straddle the legs to scale it

Name: Front Lever Row
How to: Hold a full front lever with straight legs together and pull the chest to the bar. Lower to straight arms while holding the flat body line.
Form check: Full lever, legs together · Body parallel to the floor · No hip pike

Name: Front Lever Row (Advanced Tuck)
How to: Row while holding an advanced tuck front lever with the knees opened away from the chest and the hips high.
Form check: Open the tuck · Hips stay high · Pull the chest to the bar

Name: Front Lever Row (One Leg)
How to: Row from a front lever with one leg extended and the other tucked. Swap which leg extends between sets.
Form check: One leg long, one tucked · Hips stay level · Even work on both sides

Name: Front Lever Row (Straddle)
How to: Hold a straddle front lever with the legs wide and row the chest toward the bar. Keep the body flat and the arms straight at the bottom.
Form check: Legs wide to lighten the lever · Body flat · Straight arms between reps

Name: Front Lever Row (Tuck)
How to: Hold a tuck front lever and pull the chest toward the bar while keeping the knees tucked and the back flat. Lower to straight arms without losing the shape.
Form check: Hold the tuck through the pull · Back stays parallel to the floor · Straight arms at the bottom

Name: Front Raise (Band)
How to: Stand on the middle of the band holding an end in each hand in front of your thighs. Raise the arms straight out in front to shoulder height, then lower slowly against the band.
Form check: Raise only to shoulder height · No swinging or leaning back · Keep the arms nearly straight

Name: Front Raise (Barbell)
How to: Hold a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip about shoulder width. Raise it straight out in front to shoulder height with nearly straight arms, then lower under control.
Form check: Stop at shoulder height · Keep the torso still, no swinging · Go lighter than you expect, the lever is long

Name: Front Raise (Cable)
How to: Face away from a low pulley gripping the single handle with one hand, arm hanging straight in front of your thigh. Raise the cable forward and up to shoulder height with a slight elbow bend. Lower it back down under control.
Form check: Raise to shoulder height · Don't lean back · Keep the cable taut

Name: Front Raise (Dumbbell)
How to: Sit against an incline bench set to 30 to 60 degrees, holding a dumbbell in each hand with arms straight down and palms facing back. Raise both arms forward to shoulder height. Lower them back down slowly.
Form check: Keep your back on the pad · Raise straight to the front

Name: Front Raise (Suspension)
How to: Hold the handles and lean back with your arms in front of you and your body straight. Raise your arms overhead to pull yourself upright, then lower back to the lean under control.
Form check: Body stays in one straight line · Arms stay nearly straight · Walk the feet back to reduce the load

Name: Front Squat
How to: Rack the bar across the front of the shoulders with the elbows high, take a shoulder-width stance and brace. Sit straight down between the hips keeping the torso as upright as possible, then drive up through the mid-foot.
Form check: Elbows up, chest tall, don't let them drop · keep the torso vertical · sit between the hips, knees tracking over the toes · brace hard before each rep

Name: Full Squat
How to: Stand with feet a little wider than your hips and toes turned slightly out. Sit down between your heels as deep as you can while keeping the back flat and heels down, then stand back up.
Form check: Heels stay down the whole way · Knees track over the toes · Go only as deep as the back stays flat

Name: Glute Bridge
How to: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, heels close to your hips. Drive through the heels to lift the hips until your body forms a straight line from knees to shoulders, then lower slowly.
Form check: Squeeze the glutes at the top · Ribs stay down, do not arch the back · Drive through the heels

Name: Glute Ham Raise
How to: Set your feet against the footplate between the rollers and lie facedown with your knees just behind the pad. Keep your back arched and body straight from knees to head. Lower your torso under control, then drive your toes into the plate and contract the hamstrings to pull back up.
Form check: Straight line, knees to head · Drive the toes into the plate · Control the descent

Name: Glute Kickback (Machine)
How to: Set the pad against the back of one thigh and hold the handles with your torso upright. Push the leg back and up by squeezing the glute, then return under control without letting the stack drop.
Form check: Push with the glute, do not arch the back · Torso stays still · Return slowly rather than letting it snap back

Name: Glute Kickback on Floor
How to: Start on hands and knees with a flat back. Drive one heel toward the ceiling by squeezing the glute, keeping the knee bent, then lower it back without touching down.
Form check: Keep the back flat, do not arch to go higher · Hips stay square · Push through the heel

Name: Goblet Squat
How to: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically against the chest. Sit straight down between the hips until the elbows brush the inside of the knees, then stand back up tall.
Form check: Chest up, weight tight to the body · sit between the hips, heels flat · elbows inside the knees at the bottom · brace the core throughout

Name: Good Morning (Barbell)
How to: Set a light bar across your upper back and stand with feet hip width and knees slightly bent. Push the hips straight back and fold forward until you feel the hamstrings load, then drive the hips forward to stand.
Form check: Start much lighter than you think · Flat back throughout · Push the hips back rather than bending the knees

Name: Gorilla Row (Kettlebell)
How to: Stand over two kettlebells with a wide stance and hinge down with a flat back to grip both. Row one to your hip while the other stays on the floor supporting you, then lower it and switch sides.
Form check: Keep the torso flat and still · Row to the hip, elbow drives back · The resting bell takes your weight, do not twist

Name: Hack Squat
How to: Set your shoulders and back against the pad with feet shoulder-width on the platform. Lower under control until the thighs are at least parallel, then press up through the heels without locking the knees hard.
Form check: Keep the whole back flat against the pad · knees track over the toes, don't cave in · control the descent · stop just short of locking the knees

Name: Hack Squat (Machine)
How to: Set your shoulders under the pads with your feet mid platform and release the safeties. Lower until your thighs are at least parallel by bending the knees, then press back up without locking out hard.
Form check: Whole foot stays on the platform · Back flat against the pad · Do not slam the knees straight at the top

Name: Hammer Curl (Band)
How to: Stand on the band holding an end in each hand with palms facing each other. Curl the hands to shoulder height keeping the thumbs up, then lower slowly against the band.
Form check: Palms stay facing each other · Elbows pinned at the sides · Resist the band on the way down

Name: Hammer Curl (Cable)
How to: Attach a rope to a low pulley and hold one end in each hand with palms facing each other. Curl the rope up to shoulder height keeping the thumbs up, then lower against the cable.
Form check: Neutral grip, thumbs up throughout · Elbows stay at the sides · Keep tension at the bottom, do not rest

Name: Hammer Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Rest both upper arms on a preacher bench and hold a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing each other. Lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended, then curl them up until your biceps contract. Keep the neutral grip throughout.
Form check: Keep palms facing each other, no twist · Upper arms flat on the pad

Name: Handstand Hold
How to: Kick or press up into a handstand against a wall with your hands about shoulder width. Push the floor away, stack the hips over the shoulders and hold, breathing steadily.
Form check: Push hard through the shoulders · Ribs down, do not arch the back · Come down before the shoulders give out

Name: Handstand Push Up
How to: Kick up to a wall handstand with the hands on parallettes or blocks. Lower until the head passes below the hands, then press all the way back to a locked out handstand.
Form check: Full range below the hands · Lock the elbows at the top · Keep the body straight, not arched

Name: Handstand Push-Up (Freestanding)
How to: Hold a freestanding handstand, lower to full depth, and press back to straight arms with no wall support. Correct the balance with the fingers through the whole rep.
Form check: No wall at any point · Full depth then full lockout · Keep the body line tight

Name: Hang Clean
How to: Hold the bar at mid-thigh with a shoulder-width overhand or hook grip, back flat and torso leaning slightly forward. Aggressively extend the hips, knees, and ankles, then pull under the bar and catch it in a front-rack squat.
Form check: Lean the torso slightly over the bar · Triple-extend explosively · Keep the bar brushing the thighs · Snap elbows into the front rack

Name: Hang Snatch
How to: Take a wide overhand or hook grip with the bar at the hips, feet under the hips and turned out, spine extended and chest up. Violently extend the hips, knees, and ankles, then pull under and catch the bar overhead in a squat.
Form check: Take a wide grip at the hips · Keep the bar close on the pull · Extend hips, knees, and ankles · Punch under to lockout in a squat

Name: Hanging Bent-Leg Raise
How to: From a hang, straighten the legs a little and lift the thighs above hip height. Tuck the pelvis at the top, then lower with control and stop any swing before the next rep.
Form check: Thighs above hip height · Tuck the pelvis at the top · Stay quiet on the bar

Name: Hanging Knee Raise
How to: Hang from a bar with straight arms and pull the shoulders down away from the ears. Lift the knees toward the chest and lower them under control without swinging.
Form check: Pull the shoulders down first · No swing · Lower slower than you lift

Name: Hanging Leg Raise
How to: Hang from the bar with straight arms and the shoulders pulled down. Raise your straight legs until they are at least parallel with the floor, then lower them under control without swinging.
Form check: No swinging between reps · Tuck the pelvis as the legs come up · Bend the knees to scale it down

Name: Hanging Straight-Leg Raise
How to: Hang with straight legs together and lift them until they are at least parallel to the floor. Lower slowly and let the swing settle before starting the next rep.
Form check: Straight legs to horizontal or higher · Lower with control · Reset the swing between reps

Name: Headstand Push-Up (Freestanding)
How to: Kick up to a freestanding handstand and lower under control until the head touches the floor. Press back up while making small balance corrections with the fingers.
Form check: Balance with the fingertips · Lower under control · Bail to the side if you lose it

Name: Headstand Push-Up (Wall)
How to: Set up in a wall handstand and lower until the head touches the floor between the hands. Press back to straight arms while the wall keeps you upright.
Form check: Head and hands make a triangle · Press evenly with both arms · Keep the ribs down

Name: Headstand Push-Up (Wall, Eccentric)
How to: Kick up to a handstand with the heels on the wall. Lower slowly until the head touches the floor between the hands, then come down from the wall and reset instead of pressing back up.
Form check: Three to five seconds down · Head lands between the hands · Come off the wall to reset

Name: Heel Taps
How to: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat and shoulder-width apart, and arms extended at your sides. Crunch your torso up and to one side, reaching your hand toward that heel. Return to center, then bend to the other side and touch that heel.
Form check: Crunch to the side · Reach for your heel

Name: Hex Press (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie on a bench holding two hexagonal dumbbells pressed together over your chest. Keeping them squeezed together, lower to the chest and press straight back up while maintaining the pressure.
Form check: Keep the dumbbells pressed together · Elbows tucked close to the body · Press straight up over the chest

Name: High Knee Skips
How to: Skip forward driving one knee up to hip height while the opposite arm swings up. Stay on the balls of your feet and alternate legs in a steady rhythm.
Form check: Drive the knee to hip height · Stay tall, do not lean back · Land on the ball of the foot

Name: High Knees
How to: Run on the spot bringing each knee up to hip height as fast as you can. Stay on the balls of your feet and pump the arms in time with the legs.
Form check: Knees come up to hip height · Stay tall through the torso · Quick light contacts on the balls of the feet

Name: HIIT
How to: Alternate hard intervals with easy recovery periods on any cardio machine or with bodyweight moves. Work close to your limit during the hard interval, then recover fully before the next one.
Form check: Go genuinely hard on the work interval · Recover fully between rounds · Keep the work to rest ratio consistent

Name: Hiking
How to: Walk a route with varied terrain and elevation at a pace you can hold for the whole session. Shorten the stride going uphill and control the descent through the legs.
Form check: Shorten the stride going uphill · Control the descent, do not run down · Keep a pace you can hold for the session

Name: Hip Abduction (Machine)
How to: Sit in the machine with the pads against the outside of your knees and your back flat on the seat. Push the knees apart against the resistance, pause at the widest point, then return slowly.
Form check: Back stays flat on the pad · Push the knees apart, do not lean back · Return slowly rather than letting it snap shut

Name: Hip Adduction (Machine)
How to: Sit with the pads against the inside of your knees and your legs open at a comfortable stretch. Squeeze the knees together, pause, then let them open slowly back to the stretch.
Form check: Start from a stretch you can control · Squeeze the knees fully together · Open slowly, no bouncing at the end

Name: Hip Thrust
How to: Sit with your upper back against a bench and your feet flat on the floor about shoulder width. Drive through the heels to lift the hips until your torso is parallel to the floor, then lower under control.
Form check: Bench sits under the shoulder blades · Tuck the chin and keep the ribs down · Squeeze the glutes hard at the top

Name: Hip Thrust (Barbell)
How to: Sit with the upper back on a bench and the bar across the hips. Drive through the heels to lift the hips to a straight line from knees to shoulders, then lower under control.
Form check: Tuck the chin and keep the ribs down · drive through the heels · squeeze the glutes hard at lockout · don't hyperextend the lower back at the top

Name: Hip Thrust (Machine)
How to: Sit in the machine with the pad across your hips and your feet flat on the platform. Drive the hips up until the body is level, squeeze at the top, then lower under control.
Form check: Feet flat and about shoulder width · Ribs down, do not arch the back · Full squeeze at the top before lowering

Name: Hollow Rock
How to: Lie on your back and press the lower back into the floor, then lift the shoulders and legs to make a shallow banana shape. Rock back and forth along the spine without losing that shape.
Form check: Lower back stays pressed to the floor · Rock as one rigid shape · Bend the knees to make it easier

Name: Incline Bench Press (Barbell)
How to: Lie back on an incline bench and grip the bar at medium width. Unrack it and hold it straight over your upper chest with arms locked. Lower the bar slowly to your upper chest, then drive it back up until your arms lock out.
Form check: Grip at medium width · Lower to your upper chest · Keep shoulder blades pinned

Name: Incline Bench Press (Dumbbell)
How to: On a 30-45 degree incline, start with the dumbbells at the upper chest, palms forward. Press up and slightly together until the arms are extended, then lower under control to a full stretch.
Form check: Keep the shoulder blades pulled back and down · lower to a controlled stretch, don't bounce · elbows around 45 degrees, not flared to 90 · press in a slight arc toward the top

Name: Incline Bench Press (Smith Machine)
How to: Set an incline bench under the Smith machine, with the bar set where your arms are almost fully extended. Lie back and grip slightly wider than shoulder width, then unrack. Lower the bar to your upper chest, then press up and slightly back to lockout.
Form check: Set the bar over upper chest · Grip just outside shoulders · Drive up and slightly back

Name: Incline Chest Fly (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie back on a bench set to around thirty degrees holding dumbbells above your chest with a soft elbow bend. Open the arms in a wide arc until you feel the stretch, then bring them back together.
Form check: Keep the elbow angle fixed throughout · Open only as far as is comfortable · Lighter than a press, the lever is long

Name: Incline Chest Press (Machine)
How to: Sit in the incline press with your back flat on the pad and the handles level with your upper chest. Press forward and up until your arms are almost straight, then return to a stretch.
Form check: Handles line up with the upper chest · Stop just short of locking out · Keep the shoulder blades pinned back

Name: Incline Push Ups
How to: Put the hands on a bench, box or bar with the body in a straight line. Lower the chest to the surface and press back up, lowering the hand height as you get stronger.
Form check: Lower hands means harder · Straight line from head to heels · Chest touches each rep

Name: Inverted Row (Archer)
How to: Set up with the body fully parallel to the floor under the bar or rings. Pull the chest to the bar, pause, then lower to straight arms.
Form check: Body parallel to the floor · Pause at the top · No sagging hips

Name: Inverted Row (Bent Legs)
How to: Hang under a bar with the knees bent and the feet flat on the floor. Pull the chest to the bar keeping the body in one line, then lower to straight arms.
Form check: Knees bent to lighten the load · Chest touches the bar · Hips stay up

Name: Inverted Row (Feet Elevated)
How to: Put the feet on a box so the body sits close to horizontal under the bar. Pull the chest to the bar and lower slowly without letting the hips drop.
Form check: Feet elevated to the bar height · Hips stay lifted · Chest to the bar each rep

Name: Inverted Row (Incline)
How to: Set a bar or rings at chest height and hold on with the body almost upright. Walk the feet forward a little and pull the chest to the bar, then lower under control.
Form check: Body near upright · Pull the chest to the bar · Squeeze the shoulder blades

Name: Inverted Row (One Arm)
How to: Set up horizontally under the bar and row with a single arm while the body stays rigid and square. Switch arms between sets.
Form check: One hand only · Resist the twist · Body stays parallel to the floor

Name: Inverted Row (One Arm, Assisted)
How to: Row horizontally with most of the load on one arm while the other hand gives light support on the bar or a strap. Switch sides between sets.
Form check: One arm does most of the work · Support hand stays light · Keep the hips square

Name: Inverted Row (Straight Legs)
How to: Hang under the bar with straight legs and the heels on the floor at roughly forty five degrees. Pull the chest to the bar and lower with control.
Form check: Straight legs, heels down · One line from head to heels · Full arm extension at the bottom

Name: Inverted Row (Weighted)
How to: Add external load with a vest or plates while keeping the body rigid. Pull the chest to the bar or rings, then lower to straight arms.
Form check: Record added load only · Body angle stays fixed · Chest reaches the hands · Control the descent
Equipment: Bar or gymnastic rings; weight vest or plates

Name: Inverted Row (Wide Grip)
How to: Row from the horizontal position with the hands set wider than shoulder width. Pull the chest to the bar and squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
Form check: Wider grip loads the upper back · Squeeze the shoulder blades · Keep the body flat

Name: Iso-Lateral Chest Press (Machine)
How to: Sit with your back on the pad and grip both handles at chest height. Press one arm at a time or both together, keeping the torso square, then return under control to a chest stretch.
Form check: Do not twist the torso toward the working arm · Press each side through the same range · Return to a stretch, not a rest

Name: Iso-Lateral High Row (Machine)
How to: Sit with your chest against the pad and reach up to grip the high handles. Pull one handle down and back toward your hip, driving the elbow low, then return to a full stretch overhead.
Form check: Chest stays on the pad · Drive the elbow down and back · Let the shoulder blade travel at the top

Name: Iso-Lateral Low Row
How to: Sit with your chest on the pad and grip the low handles with your arms extended. Pull one handle back to your ribs by driving the elbow behind you, then return to a full stretch.
Form check: Chest stays against the pad · Pull to the ribs, elbow drives back · Full stretch at the front of each rep

Name: Iso-Lateral Row (Machine)
How to: Sit with your chest against the pad and take one handle in each hand at arms length. Row one side back until the elbow passes your torso, then return under control and repeat on the other side.
Form check: Torso stays square, do not rotate into the pull · Squeeze the shoulder blade at the back · Full stretch at the front

Name: Jack Knife (Suspension)
How to: Set up in a push up position with both feet in the suspension cradles and your body straight. Draw the knees toward your chest by folding at the hips, then extend the legs back to the straight plank.
Form check: Body straight before you start folding · Hips rise as the knees come in · Return slowly, do not let the hips sag

Name: Jackknife Sit Up
How to: Lie flat with your arms extended overhead and legs straight. Exhale and raise your legs and torso at the same time, reaching your hands toward your feet so your body forms a V. Lower your arms and legs back down under control.
Form check: Raise legs and torso as one · Keep legs straight, not bent · Meet hands to feet up top

Name: JM Press (Barbell)
How to: Lie on a bench holding the bar over your chest with a close grip. Lower it toward your chin by letting the elbows travel forward, stopping just above the collarbone, then press back up with the triceps.
Form check: Elbows travel forward, not out to the sides · Bar comes down toward the chin · Start light, this one is fussy

Name: Jump Rope
How to: Hold the handles at hip height and turn the rope with the wrists rather than the arms. Jump just high enough to clear the rope, landing on the balls of your feet with soft knees.
Form check: Turn the rope with the wrists · Jump only an inch or two · Land soft on the balls of the feet

Name: Jump Shrug
How to: Hold a barbell at arms length in front of your thighs. Dip slightly, then extend the hips and ankles explosively and shrug the shoulders hard so you leave the floor, landing softly in the same stance.
Form check: Extend the hips before the shrug · Arms stay straight, do not pull · Land soft in the same spot

Name: Jump Squat
How to: Stand with feet shoulder width and squat down to around parallel. Jump straight up as high as you can, then land softly and absorb straight back into the next squat.
Form check: Land soft with bent knees · Chest stays up on landing · Absorb into the squat rather than stopping dead

Name: Jumping Jack
How to: Start standing with feet together and arms at your sides. Jump the feet out wide while sweeping the arms overhead, then jump back to the start in a steady rhythm.
Form check: Land on the balls of the feet · Arms travel all the way overhead · Keep a steady even rhythm

Name: Jumping Lunge
How to: Drop into a lunge with the front knee bent over your foot and the rear knee nearly touching the floor. Extend explosively through both legs to jump as high as you can, swinging the arms up. Land softly back in the lunge and absorb through both legs.
Form check: Drop into a deep lunge · Front knee stacked over the foot · Explode up through both legs · Land back in the lunge

Name: Kettlebell Clean
How to: Place a kettlebell between your feet, push your hips back, and grip it one-handed with eyes forward. Extend through the legs and hips to pull the bell up, rotating your hand around it to catch cleanly at the shoulder. Lower and repeat.
Form check: Keep the bell tight to the body · Wrap the rack, don't bang it

Name: Kettlebell Curl
How to: Hold a kettlebell in each hand by the handle with your elbows tucked at your sides. Curl them up to shoulder height, letting the bells rest against the forearms, then lower under control.
Form check: Elbows stay pinned at the sides · Let the bell settle on the forearm at the top · No swinging the torso

Name: Kettlebell Goblet Squat
How to: Stand with your feet around shoulder-width apart and hold a kettlebell close to your chest with both hands. Brace your core and squat down by bending the hips and knees while keeping your chest upright. Descend as far as you can with good control, then drive through the whole foot to stand back up.
Form check: Keep the kettlebell close to the chest · Chest stays upright · Knees track over the toes · Keep the whole foot planted · Do not let the lower back round at the bottom

Name: Kettlebell High Pull
How to: Stand in a wide sumo stance with a kettlebell between your feet and grip it with both hands, hips set back and chest up. Drive through your legs and hips to pull the kettlebell explosively up to chest height, leading with high elbows. Lower it back between your legs.
Form check: Drive through legs and hips · Explode the bell to chest height · Lead with high elbows · Keep your chest up, back flat

Name: Kettlebell Shoulder Press
How to: Clean the kettlebell to the rack position at your shoulder with the bell resting on the forearm. Press it overhead until the arm locks, then lower back to the rack under control.
Form check: Bell rests on the forearm, not the wrist · Ribs down, do not arch the back · Lock out with the bicep near the ear

Name: Kettlebell Snatch
How to: Set a kettlebell between your feet, bend the knees, and sit the hips back with eyes forward. Swing the bell back between your legs, then reverse hard and drive through the hips to punch it straight to lockout overhead in one motion.
Form check: Drive the swing with the hips · Keep the bell close on the way up · Spear the hand through at lockout

Name: Kettlebell Swing
How to: Stand with the kettlebell a step in front of you and hinge down to grip it with both hands. Hike it back between your legs, then snap the hips forward to float it up to chest height and let it swing back down.
Form check: Drive with the hips, do not lift with the arms · Bell floats, it is not raised · Keep the back flat through the hinge

Name: Kettlebell Turkish Get Up
How to: Lie on your back and press one kettlebell to a locked-out arm above your shoulder. Keeping the elbow locked and eyes on the bell, rise to your feet through a series of controlled steps. Stand fully, then reverse each step back to the floor.
Form check: Press the bell to a locked arm · Keep the elbow locked throughout · Keep your eyes on the bell · Rise and reverse one step at a time

Name: Kipping Pull Up
How to: Hang from the bar and swing between a hollow and an arch position. Time the hip drive with the pull so the momentum carries your chin over the bar, then return to the swing and repeat.
Form check: Learn strict pull ups first · Drive the hips, then pull · Keep the shoulders active on the return swing

Name: Knee Raise Parallel Bars
How to: Support yourself on the raise station with your forearms on the pads and back against the rest, legs hanging straight down. Raise your knees up toward your chest by curling your hips and contracting your abs. Lower them slowly to the hang.
Form check: Curl your hips under, not just knees · Keep your legs from swinging

Name: Kneeling Pulldown (band)
How to: Anchor the band overhead and kneel underneath it holding one end in each hand. Pull the band down to your chest by driving the elbows to your ribs, then let it rise back under control.
Form check: Kneel tall, do not sit back on the heels · Drive the elbows down to the ribs · Let the arms straighten fully at the top

Name: Kneeling Push Up
How to: Set up on your hands and knees with your hands under your shoulders and your body straight from knees to head. Lower the chest toward the floor, then press back up without letting the hips sag.
Form check: Straight line from knees to head · Hands under the shoulders · Chest leads down, hips do not sag

Name: L-Sit Hold
How to: Support on parallettes or bars with straight arms, then lift straight legs until they are parallel to the floor. Point the toes and hold with the shoulders pushed away from the ears.
Form check: Legs straight and parallel to the floor · Toes pointed · Shoulders pushed down

Name: L-Sit Hold (Advanced Tuck)
How to: From the tuck position, open the knees to roughly a right angle so the thighs move away from the chest. Hold with a flat back and the hips level with the shoulders.
Form check: Open the tuck to ninety degrees · Keep the back flat · Hips level with the shoulders

Name: L-Sit Hold (Foot-Supported)
How to: Sit with straight legs and press your hands into the floor or parallettes beside the hips. Push the shoulders down and lift the body so the heels rest lightly on the ground and carry almost no weight.
Form check: Push the floor away · Heels light, not loaded · Straight arms throughout

Name: L-Sit Hold (Straddle)
How to: Hold an L-sit and open the legs into a wide straddle. Keep both legs at hip height or higher and press the shoulders down for the whole hold.
Form check: Open the legs wide · Keep them level or higher · Straight knees

Name: L-Sit Hold (Tuck)
How to: Support yourself on parallettes or bars with straight arms and pull both knees tightly to the chest. Hold with the shoulders pressed down and the hips lifted clear of the floor.
Form check: Knees tight to the chest · Shoulders pressed down · Lift the hips, do not hang

Name: Landmine 180
How to: Hold the end of a landmine barbell overhead with both hands and your arms nearly straight. Rotate the bar from one side to the other in an arc, turning through the hips and pivoting the feet.
Form check: Turn through the hips, not just the arms · Pivot the back foot each way · Control the arc, do not let it drop

Name: Landmine Row
How to: Straddle a landmine barbell and hinge forward with a flat back, gripping the bar with both hands or a V handle. Row it to your chest by driving the elbows back, then lower to a full stretch.
Form check: Flat back, hinged at the hips · Pull to the lower chest · Let the shoulder blades open at the bottom

Name: Landmine Squat and Press
How to: Hold the end of a landmine bar at your chest with both hands. Squat down keeping the chest tall, then stand and press the bar up and forward in one continuous movement.
Form check: Squat and press flow as one movement · Chest stays tall in the squat · Follow the bar path forward, not straight up

Name: Lat Pulldown (Band)
How to: Anchor the band overhead and hold one end in each hand with your arms extended above you. Pull the band down until your hands reach shoulder height, then let it rise back under control.
Form check: Pull the elbows down to the ribs · Chest stays tall, avoid leaning far back · Full stretch overhead each rep

Name: Lat Pulldown (Cable)
How to: Sit with your thighs under the pads and grip the bar wider than your shoulders. Pull it down to your upper chest by driving the elbows down, then let it rise back to a full overhead stretch.
Form check: Pull to the upper chest, not behind the neck · Drive with the elbows, not the hands · Full stretch at the top

Name: Lat Pulldown (Machine)
How to: Sit with your thighs secured and grip the handles overhead. Pull them down toward your upper chest by driving the elbows down and back, then return to a full stretch.
Form check: Set the thigh pads snug before starting · Elbows drive down and back · Do not lean back to finish the rep

Name: Lat Pulldown - Close Grip (Cable)
How to: Sit with your thighs under the pads and take a narrow neutral grip on the handle. Pull it to your upper chest keeping the elbows close to the body, then return to a full stretch overhead.
Form check: Elbows stay close to the ribs · Pull to the upper chest · Let the shoulders rise at the top for a full stretch

Name: Lateral Band Walks
How to: Place a band around your legs just above the knees or ankles and sink into a quarter squat. Step sideways against the band, keeping tension the whole way, then step the trailing foot in.
Form check: Stay low in the quarter squat · Keep tension on the band, feet never touch · Toes point forward, do not turn out

Name: Lateral Box Jump
How to: Stand tall beside a short box with feet hip-width. Dip quickly into a quarter squat to load, then explode up and sideways to land on top of the box. Absorb softly in a partial squat with both feet, then step down and reset on the other side.
Form check: Quick dip, jump sideways · Land balanced on the box · Step down, don't jump down

Name: Lateral Leg Raises
How to: Lie on your side with your body in a straight line and your lower arm supporting your head. Raise the top leg as high as you can without tipping the hips back, then lower it under control.
Form check: Hips stay stacked, do not roll back · Keep the leg in line with the body · Lower slowly rather than dropping

Name: Lateral Lunge
How to: Stand tall and take a wide step out to one side. Sit the hips back and bend that knee while the other leg stays straight, then push off to return to standing.
Form check: Both feet stay flat and pointing forward · Sit the hips back, do not just bend the knee · Trailing leg stays straight

Name: Lateral Raise (Band)
How to: Stand on the middle of the band with an end in each hand at your sides. Raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder height with a slight elbow bend, then lower slowly against the band.
Form check: Stop at shoulder height · Lead with the elbows, not the hands · Do not shrug the shoulders up

Name: Lateral Raise (Cable)
How to: Place a flat bench between two opposing low pulleys and sit on it. Grab each handle with the opposite hand so the cables cross under your knees. Raise both handles out to your sides to shoulder height, then lower slowly against the tension.
Form check: Cross the cables under your knees · Raise out to shoulder height

Name: Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with a slight bend in the elbows. Raise the arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, then lower them slowly.
Form check: Raise to shoulder height, no higher · Lead with the elbows · No swinging, use a weight you can control

Name: Lateral Raise (Machine)
How to: Sit with the pads against the outside of your upper arms and your torso upright. Raise the arms out to the sides until they reach shoulder height, then lower under control.
Form check: Set the seat so the pads sit on the upper arms · Stop level with the shoulders · Do not shrug at the top

Name: Lateral Squat
How to: Stand with your feet much wider than your shoulders and your toes forward. Shift your weight to one side and sit that hip back into a squat while the other leg stays straight, then shift across.
Form check: Both feet stay flat on the floor · Sit the hip back, not just down · Keep the straight leg straight

Name: Leg Extension (Machine)
How to: Sit with the pad resting on the front of your ankles and your knees in line with the machine pivot. Straighten the legs until they are locked out, pause, then lower under control.
Form check: Line the knees up with the machine pivot · Pause at the top · Lower slowly, do not let the stack drop

Name: Leg Press (Machine)
How to: Sit in the sled with your feet shoulder width on the platform and release the safeties. Lower until your knees reach about ninety degrees, then press back without locking the knees hard.
Form check: Whole foot stays on the platform · Lower back stays on the seat, no rounding · Do not slam the knees straight

Name: Leg Press Horizontal (Machine)
How to: Sit with your back against the pad and your feet flat on the platform in front of you. Press the platform away until the legs are nearly straight, then let it return until the knees reach ninety degrees.
Form check: Back and hips stay against the pad · Stop just short of locking out · Keep the heels down on the platform

Name: Leg Raise Parallel Bars
