How to: Support yourself on the parallel bars or a captains chair with your back against the pad. Raise your straight legs to at least parallel with the floor, then lower them slowly without swinging.
Form check: No swinging between reps · Tuck the pelvis as the legs rise · Bend the knees to scale it down

Name: Low Cable Fly Crossovers
How to: Stand between two low pulleys with a handle in each hand and your palms facing forward. Sweep the arms up and together in front of your chest, then lower them back out to a stretch.
Form check: Sweep upward, finishing at chest height · Soft elbow bend throughout · Squeeze at the top before opening

Name: Low Row (Suspension)
How to: Hold the handles and walk your feet forward so you hang back with your body straight. Pull your chest to your hands by driving the elbows past your ribs, then lower back to straight arms.
Form check: Body stays in one straight line · Elbows drive back past the ribs · Walk the feet back to make it easier

Name: Lunge
How to: Stand tall and step forward into a long stride. Lower until both knees reach about ninety degrees and the back knee is just above the floor, then push through the front heel to stand.
Form check: Long stride, torso stays upright · Front shin close to vertical · Push through the front heel to return

Name: Lunge (Barbell)
How to: With the bar on the upper back, step forward and lower until the back knee is just off the floor and the front thigh is parallel. Drive through the front heel back to standing.
Form check: Torso upright, core braced · front knee stays over the foot, not past the toes · drive through the front heel · control the descent, don't drop

Name: Lunge (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and step forward into a long stride. Lower until the back knee is just above the floor, then drive through the front heel to stand back up.
Form check: Torso stays upright, do not lean over the front leg · Back knee hovers just off the floor · Drive through the front heel

Name: Lying Bent-Leg Raise
How to: Lie on your back and extend the shins so the legs are only slightly bent. Raise them until the hips are fully flexed, then lower under control with the lower back pinned down.
Form check: Longer lever, same flat back · Control the lowering · Shorten the range if the back lifts

Name: Lying Knee Raise
How to: Lie on your back with the hands beside the hips and press the lower back into the floor. Draw the knees toward the chest, then lower them slowly without letting the back arch.
Form check: Low back stays flat · Slow on the way down · Stop before the back lifts

Name: Lying Leg Curl (Machine)
How to: Lie face down with the pad resting just above your heels and your knees just off the end of the bench. Curl the heels toward your glutes as far as they go, then lower under control.
Form check: Hips stay pressed to the bench · Curl all the way, then lower slowly · Do not let the stack slam down

Name: Lying Leg Raise
How to: Lie on your back with your hands under your hips and your legs straight. Raise the legs until they are vertical, then lower them slowly without letting the lower back lift off the floor.
Form check: Lower back stays flat on the floor · Stop lowering before the back arches · Bend the knees to scale it down

Name: Lying Neck Curls
How to: Lie face up on a bench with your head hanging just off the end. Curl the chin toward your chest through the full range, then lower the head back down slowly.
Form check: Move slowly, the neck does not like speed · Full range but no forcing · Stop at once if anything pinches

Name: Lying Neck Curls (Weighted)
How to: Lie face up with your head off the end of a bench and hold a light plate on your forehead with a towel underneath. Curl the chin to the chest, then lower the head slowly.
Form check: Use a towel between the plate and the head · Very light load, slow tempo · Stop at once if anything pinches

Name: Lying Neck Extension
How to: Lie face down on a bench with your head hanging off the end. Raise the head by looking forward and up through the full comfortable range, then lower it back down slowly.
Form check: Slow and controlled both ways · Stay inside a comfortable range · Stop at once if anything pinches

Name: Lying Neck Extension (Weighted)
How to: Lie face down with your head off the end of a bench and hold a light plate on the back of your head with a towel underneath. Raise the head up, then lower it slowly.
Form check: Towel between the plate and the head · Start with the lightest plate · Slow tempo, never jerk the movement

Name: Lying Straight-Leg Raise
How to: Lie flat with straight legs held together. Lift them until they point at the ceiling, then lower slowly until the heels hover just above the floor with the back still flat.
Form check: Straight knees · Heels stop just off the floor · Keep the back flat all set

Name: Meadows Rows (Barbell)
How to: Stand side on at the loaded end of a landmine barbell and hinge over with a flat back, gripping the sleeve with the outside hand. Row it up to your hip, then lower to a full stretch.
Form check: Hinge over with a flat back · Pull the elbow high and back · Let the shoulder blade stretch at the bottom

Name: Mountain Climber
How to: Set up in a push up position with your hands under your shoulders and your body straight. Drive one knee toward your chest, then switch legs quickly while the hips stay level.
Form check: Hips stay level, do not bounce up and down · Hands stay under the shoulders · Quick light foot contacts

Name: Muscle Up
How to: Pull explosively until the bar or rings reach the lower chest. Roll the shoulders forward over the top and press out to a locked support with no leg swing.
Form check: Pull to the lower chest, not the chin · Lean over the bar at the transition · No kip

Name: Muscle Up (Eccentric)
How to: Start at the top in a straight arm support and lower slowly through the transition until you finish in a hang. Take the transition as slowly as you can control it.
Form check: Slowest through the transition · Keep the rings or bar close · Finish in a full hang

Name: Muscle Up (Kipping)
How to: From a hang, swing the legs forward and drive the hips up while pulling the bar toward the waist. Roll the shoulders over the top and press out to a straight arm support.
Form check: Time the hip drive with the pull · Roll the shoulders forward early · Finish with straight arms

Name: Negative Pull Up
How to: Jump or step so your chin starts above the bar. Lower yourself for three to five seconds until the arms are straight, then step down and reset for the next rep.
Form check: Three to five seconds down · Finish with straight arms · Step down and reset each rep

Name: Nordic Hamstrings Curls
How to: Anchor the heels under a bar or have a partner hold them. Keep the hips straight and lower the body toward the floor as slowly as you can, catching with the hands.
Form check: Hips stay open, not folded · Lower as slowly as possible · Catch with the hands

Name: Oblique Crunch
How to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and dropped to one side and your hands light beside your head. Curl the shoulders off the floor toward the ceiling, then lower under control and switch sides.
Form check: Curl up rather than twisting the neck · Hands rest light, no pulling on the head · Do the same reps on both sides

Name: One Arm Push Up
How to: Set the feet wide and put one hand under the chest with the other behind the back. Lower the chest to the floor and press up while keeping the hips square.
Form check: Feet wide for balance · Hips stay square to the floor · Chest touches the floor

Name: One-Arm One-Leg Plank
How to: From a forearm plank, lift one arm and the opposite leg a few inches off the floor. Hold without letting the hips rotate, then set them down and switch sides.
Form check: Lift opposite arm and leg · Keep the hips square to the floor · Short strict holds

Name: Overhead Curl (Cable)
How to: Set both pulleys high and grab a handle in each hand. Stand tall between them with arms extended out at shoulder height, palms up. Curl both hands toward your ears until your biceps peak, then straighten your arms back out.
Form check: Keep elbows high at shoulder level · Curl your knuckles toward your ears · Move only the forearms

Name: Overhead Dumbbell Lunge
How to: Hold a dumbbell locked out overhead with one or both arms and step forward into a long stride. Lower until the back knee nearly touches, then drive back to standing with the weight still overhead.
Form check: Keep the arm locked and the ribs down · Torso stays upright · Start much lighter than a normal lunge

Name: Overhead Press (Barbell)
How to: Hold the bar at shoulder height with your grip just outside your shoulders and your elbows slightly in front. Press it overhead in a straight line, moving your head back out of the way, then lower to the shoulders.
Form check: Squeeze the glutes so the back does not arch · Move the head back, not the bar around it · Finish with the bar over the mid foot

Name: Overhead Press (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing forward. Press them overhead until the arms lock out, then lower back to shoulder height under control.
Form check: Ribs down, do not arch the lower back · Press up, not out in front · Lower all the way to the shoulders

Name: Overhead Press (Smith Machine)
How to: Set a bench with back support under the Smith bar and sit so the bar sits just above your shoulders. Unrack it with a overhand grip and press the bar straight up until your arms extend. Lower under control to the top of your chest.
Form check: Follow the fixed bar path up · Lower the bar to upper chest

Name: Overhead Squat
How to: Take a wide snatch grip and press the barbell to full lockout overhead, feet slightly wider than the shoulders. Push the bar back so it sits over your midfoot. Squat down as deep as mobility allows while keeping the bar overhead, then drive up.
Form check: Wide snatch grip, elbows locked · Keep the bar over midfoot · Actively push the bar up · Squat deep, bar stays back

Name: Pause Squat (Barbell)
How to: Squat down with the bar on your back until your thighs are at least parallel and hold that bottom position for two to three seconds. Stay tight through the pause, then drive up out of the hole.
Form check: Hold two to three seconds at the bottom · Stay braced, do not relax in the pause · Drive up without rocking forward

Name: Pendlay Row (Barbell)
How to: Set your torso parallel to the floor with the bar resting on the ground. Row it explosively to your lower chest, then return it all the way to the floor and reset before the next rep.
Form check: Torso stays parallel the whole set · Bar returns to the floor each rep · Do not raise the chest to pull the bar

Name: Pendulum Squat (Machine)
How to: Set your shoulders under the pads and your feet on the platform, then release the safeties. Lower along the machine arc until your thighs pass parallel, then drive back up through the whole foot.
Form check: Let the machine arc guide the path · Whole foot stays down · Do not bounce out of the bottom

Name: Pike Push-Up (Feet Elevated)
How to: Put the feet on a box so the hips stack higher over the shoulders. Lower the head toward the floor between the hands and press back up with the elbows tracking forward.
Form check: Higher box means more vertical load · Stack the hips over the shoulders · Head between the hands

Name: Pike Pushup
How to: Start in a pushup position and walk the feet in so the hips lift high and the body makes an upside down V. Bend the elbows to lower the crown of the head toward the floor, then press back up.
Form check: Hips high, body in a V · Head lowers between the hands · Elbows track forward

Name: Pilates
How to: Move through a sequence of controlled mat exercises that work the deep core, breathing steadily with each movement. Keep the pace slow and precise rather than chasing repetitions.
Form check: Move slowly and precisely · Breathe with the movement, do not hold your breath · Quality over repetitions

Name: Pinwheel Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing your body. Curl one dumbbell up across your chest toward the opposite shoulder, then lower it and repeat on the other side.
Form check: Neutral grip, thumb stays up · Curl across the body, not straight up · Elbow stays pinned at your side

Name: Pistol Squat
How to: Stand on one leg with the other held straight out in front. Lower all the way to the bottom and stand back up with no support and no bouncing.
Form check: Full depth on one leg · Free leg never touches · Heel stays flat

Name: Pistol Squat (Box)
How to: Stand on one leg in front of a box, hold the free leg forward, and lower until the hips lightly touch the box before standing on the same leg. Reduce box height as strength improves.
Form check: Touch rather than sit · Knee tracks over toes · Free foot stays clear · No rocking for momentum

Name: Pistol Squat (Counterweighted)
How to: Hold a light plate or dumbbell out in front of the chest to balance the load. Lower on one leg to the bottom and stand back up.
Form check: Counterweight helps balance · Free leg straight in front · Drop the weight as balance improves

Name: Planche
How to: Hold the body horizontal with the legs together and the arms locked straight. The whole body stays in one line parallel to the floor.
Form check: Legs together and straight · Body parallel to the floor · Push down hard through the whole hold

Name: Planche (Advanced Tuck)
How to: From the tuck planche, open the knees so the thighs move away from the chest and flatten the back. Hold with the hips level and the arms locked straight.
Form check: Open the tuck, flatten the back · Hips level with the shoulders · Keep pushing the floor away

Name: Planche (Straddle)
How to: Hold a straight-arm planche with the legs separated to shorten the lever. Keep the body horizontal and gradually narrow the straddle as strength improves.
Form check: Arms locked · Hips level with shoulders · No piking · Point the toes

Name: Planche (Tuck)
How to: Support on the floor or parallettes with straight arms, lean forward, and pull both knees to the chest with the hips lifted to shoulder height. Hold with a rounded upper back.
Form check: Hips up to shoulder height · Knees tight to the chest · Round the upper back and push down

Name: Planche Lean
How to: Start in a straight-arm push-up position with the hands slightly turned out. Lean the shoulders forward past the wrists while keeping the body rigid and the shoulder blades protracted.
Form check: Arms locked · Shoulders ahead of wrists · Push the floor away · No hip sag

Name: Planche Lean (Tuck)
How to: Hold a deep planche lean and lift one knee at a time toward the chest so both feet leave the floor briefly. Keep the shoulders forward and the arms locked.
Form check: Lean first, then tuck · Both feet leave the floor · Arms stay straight

Name: Planche Push-Up
How to: Hold a full planche with the legs together and the body horizontal. Lower the chest toward the floor and press back to straight arms with the feet never touching down.
Form check: Legs together and straight · Body parallel to the floor · Feet never touch

Name: Planche Push-Up (Advanced Tuck)
How to: Hold an advanced tuck planche with the back flat and the knees away from the chest. Lower under control and press back up while keeping the hips level.
Form check: Flat back throughout · Hips level with the shoulders · Stop the set when the tuck closes

Name: Planche Push-Up (Straddle)
How to: Hold a straddle planche with the legs wide and the body horizontal. Bend the arms to lower, then press back to straight arms without dropping the hips.
Form check: Legs wide to shorten the lever · Body stays parallel to the floor · Full lockout at the top

Name: Planche Push-Up (Tuck)
How to: Hold a tuck planche with the knees at the chest and the hips high. Bend the arms to lower the chest, then press back up without letting the feet touch down.
Form check: Feet never touch the floor · Hips stay high · Short sets

Name: Plank
How to: Rest on the forearms and toes with the elbows under the shoulders. Brace the abdominals and glutes to hold a straight line from head to heels for the prescribed time.
Form check: Elbows under shoulders · Ribs down · No sagging or piking · Breathe steadily

Name: Plank Pushup
How to: Start in a forearm plank with your body straight. Press up onto one hand at a time until you are in a push up position, then lower back to the forearms one arm at a time, alternating the lead.
Form check: Hips stay level, minimize the rocking · Alternate which arm leads · Widen the feet to make it steadier

Name: Plate Curl
How to: Hold a weight plate by the edges in front of your thighs with your elbows tucked at your sides. Curl it up to shoulder height, squeeze, then lower under control.
Form check: Grip the rim, do not use the handles · Elbows stay pinned at the sides · No swinging the torso

Name: Plate Front Raise
How to: Stand tall gripping a weight plate at the 3 and 9 o'clock edges, palms facing each other, arms extended down with a slight elbow bend. Raise the plate forward to shoulder height. Lower it back down under control.
Form check: Grip at 3 and 9 · Don't rock the torso

Name: Plate Press
How to: Hold a weight plate flat between both palms at chest height with your elbows out. Press it straight forward until the arms are extended, then bring it back to the chest while squeezing the whole time.
Form check: Squeeze the plate hard throughout · Press straight forward at chest height · Keep the shoulders down, not shrugged

Name: Plate Squeeze (Svend Press)
How to: Press two plates together between your palms at chest height. Push them straight out in front of you while squeezing hard, hold briefly, then bring them back to the chest.
Form check: The squeeze is the exercise, not the weight · Press straight out at chest height · Keep the elbows up, not dropped

Name: Power Clean
How to: From a deadlift setup, pull the bar explosively past the knees, extend the hips, ankles and knees, then whip the elbows through to catch the bar on the front of the shoulders in a partial squat.
Form check: Keep the bar close to the body · explode through the hips, knees and ankles · fast elbows to rack the bar · catch soft in a quarter squat

Name: Power Snatch
How to: Stand over the bar with a wide grip, feet under your hips, hips down and chest up. Pull the bar from the floor and accelerate it past your hips with a powerful snap of the hips and knees. Pull yourself under and catch it locked out overhead in a partial squat, then stand.
Form check: Wide grip, bar brushing close · Accelerate past the hips · Full snap of hips and knees · Punch under to lockout

Name: Preacher Curl (Barbell)
How to: Sit at the preacher bench with your upper arms flat on the pad and grip an EZ or straight bar. Curl the bar up to shoulder height, then lower until the arms are almost straight.
Form check: Upper arms stay flat on the pad · Lower almost to straight, but stay in control · Do not bounce out of the bottom

Name: Preacher Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Rest both upper arms on a preacher bench and hold a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing each other. Lower the dumbbells until your arms are fully extended, then curl them up until your biceps contract. Keep the neutral grip throughout.
Form check: Keep palms facing each other, no twist · Upper arms flat on the pad

Name: Preacher Curl (Machine)
How to: Sit with your upper arms flat on the pad and grip the handles with the arms extended. Curl up to shoulder height, squeeze, then lower until the arms are nearly straight again.
Form check: Set the seat so the armpits reach the top of the pad · Upper arms stay flat · Lower slower than you lift

Name: Press Under
How to: Hold a light barbell at your shoulders. Dip the knees and punch the bar overhead while dropping your body underneath it into a partial squat, then stand tall with the bar locked out.
Form check: Drop under the bar, do not just press it up · Finish with the bar over the mid foot · Keep it light, this is a technique drill

Name: Pull Up
How to: Hang from the bar with an overhand grip at shoulder width. Pull until the chin clears the bar, then lower all the way to straight arms under control.
Form check: Chin fully over the bar · Lower to straight arms · Keep the body from swinging

Name: Pull Up (Archer)
How to: Pull up with a wide grip and travel toward one hand while the opposite arm stays straight along the bar. Alternate sides each rep.
Form check: One arm straight like drawing a bow · Pull high before you shift · Alternate sides

Name: Pull Up (Assisted)
How to: Set the assist machine or loop a band under your knee and grip the bar overhand, wider than your shoulders. Pull until your chin clears the bar, then lower to fully straight arms.
Form check: Use the least assistance you can manage · Chin clears the bar · Lower all the way to straight arms

Name: Pull Up (Band)
How to: Loop a band under the knee or foot, or rest one foot on a low box. Pull to full range with the chin over the bar and use only as much help as you need.
Form check: Use the least help that works · Full range every rep · Drop the assistance as you get stronger

Name: Pull Up (Belly Button)
How to: Pull as high as you can while leaning back hard so the bar travels toward the navel. Keep the pull smooth rather than kipping into position.
Form check: Bar aims for the navel · Big lean back · No kip

Name: Pull Up (Chest to Bar)
How to: Pull explosively while leaning back so the bar meets the lower chest. Keep the elbows driving down and behind you at the top.
Form check: Bar touches the lower chest · Lean back at the top · Drive the elbows down

Name: Pull Up (Close Grip)
How to: Take an overhand grip narrower than shoulder width. Pull to the bar keeping the elbows close to the body, then lower to a full hang.
Form check: Hands inside shoulder width · Elbows brush the ribs · Full hang at the bottom

Name: Pull Up (False Grip)
How to: Hook the wrists over the rings or bar so the heel of the hand sits on top of the grip. Pull until the rings reach the lower chest while holding that wrist position throughout.
Form check: Heel of the hand on top of the ring · Pull to the lower chest · Expect sore wrists at first

Name: Pull Up (L-Sit)
How to: Hold both legs straight out in front at hip height, then perform full pull ups without letting the legs drop.
Form check: Legs stay parallel to the floor · No swinging · Drop the set when the legs sag

Name: Pull Up (One Arm, Eccentric)
How to: Start at the top with one arm and the chin over the bar. Lower as slowly as you can through the full range until the arm is straight.
Form check: Start at the top · Fight the whole way down · Stop when the descent turns into a drop

Name: Pull Up (Typewriter)
How to: Pull to the top with a wide grip, then shift sideways over one hand while the other arm straightens. Move back across the bar and lower under control.
Form check: Stay high while you travel · Straighten the trailing arm · Even reps on both sides

Name: Pull Up (Weighted)
How to: Attach additional load with a belt or vest. Start from a full hang, pull until the chin clears the bar, and lower under control.
Form check: Record added load only · Full hang · Chin over bar · No kipping
Equipment: Pull-up bar; weight belt or vest

Name: Pullover (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie on a bench holding one dumbbell over your chest with both hands and a soft elbow bend. Lower it back behind your head until you feel the stretch, then pull it back over your chest.
Form check: Keep the elbow angle fixed · Go only as far back as is comfortable · Ribs stay down, do not arch off the bench

Name: Pullover (Machine)
How to: Sit in the machine with the pads on your upper arms and the belt fastened. Pull the arms down and forward until the elbows reach your ribs, then let them rise back to a full stretch.
Form check: Drive with the elbows, not the hands · Back stays flat on the pad · Full stretch overhead each rep

Name: Push Press
How to: Hold the bar on the front of the shoulders with a shoulder-width grip and elbows up. Dip briefly at the knees, then drive explosively through the legs to launch the bar overhead and lock the arms out. Lower under control to the shoulders and reset.
Form check: Short, vertical dip, do not lean forward · drive with the legs, not just the arms · finish with the bar stacked over the mid-foot · brace the core throughout

Name: Push Up
How to: Set the hands slightly wider than the shoulders with the body in a straight line. Lower until the chest is just off the floor, then press back to locked arms.
Form check: Elbows at about forty five degrees · Hips in line with the shoulders · Full lockout at the top

Name: Push Up (Weighted)
How to: Have a partner set a plate on your upper back or wear a weight vest, then set up in a push up position. Lower the chest to just above the floor and press back up without the hips sagging.
Form check: Load sits on the upper back, not the lower · Body stays in one straight line · Full range before you add more weight

Name: Push Up - Close Grip
How to: Perform pushups keeping the elbows tucked close to the ribs the whole way down. The hands sit under the lower chest rather than out wide.
Form check: Elbows brush the ribs · Hands under the lower chest · Expect more triceps work

Name: Push-Up (Archer)
How to: Take a wide hand position and lower toward one hand while the other arm straightens out to the side. Press back up and alternate sides.
Form check: Straighten the far arm · Chest lands over the working hand · Alternate each rep

Name: Push-Up (One Arm, Incline)
How to: Place one hand on a bench or box with the other behind the back and the feet wide. Lower the chest to the surface and press back up, then switch sides.
Form check: Feet wide for balance · Lower the surface as you progress · Hips stay square

Name: Push-Up (Pseudo Planche)
How to: Place the hands lower beside the torso, lean the shoulders forward past the hands, and perform push-ups without losing the forward lean.
Form check: Shoulders remain ahead of hands · Body stays rigid · Elbows track close · Use a pain-free wrist angle

Name: Push-Up (Rings Turned Out)
How to: Set the rings just off the floor and turn them out so the palms face forward at the top. Lower to the chest and press back up, restoring the turnout each rep.
Form check: Turn the rings out at lockout · Elbows stay close · Control the wobble

Name: Push-Up (Rings Turned Out, Archer)
How to: Perform archer pushups on rings turned out at the top. Lower toward one ring while the other arm straightens, then press back and turn the rings out again.
Form check: Turnout at the top of each rep · Far arm straightens · Alternate sides

Name: Push-Up (Rings Turned Out, Pseudo Planche)
How to: On rings turned out, lean the shoulders forward and perform push-ups while keeping the rings stable and the forward lean consistent.
Form check: Rings remain turned out · Shoulders ahead of hands · No ring drift · Control the bottom

Name: Push-Up (Rings)
How to: Set the rings just off the floor and hold them at shoulder width. Lower the chest to ring height and press back up while keeping the rings from wobbling.
Form check: Rings stay under the shoulders · Full range each rep · Squeeze the rings hard

Name: Push-Up (Rings, Wide)
How to: Set the rings a few inches off the floor and take a wide hand position. Lower the chest between the rings and press back up while stopping them from drifting.
Form check: Wide hands, deeper stretch · Rings stay steady · Body in one line

Name: Push-Up (Uneven)
How to: Put one hand on a low block or ball and the other on the floor. Perform pushups so the lower arm takes most of the load, then switch sides.
Form check: Lower hand does most of the work · Keep the hips square · Even sets on both sides

Name: Push-Up (Wall)
How to: Stand an arm length from a wall and place the hands on it at chest height. Bend the elbows to bring the chest to the wall, then press back to straight arms.
Form check: Body stays in one line · Elbows at about forty five degrees · Step the feet back to make it harder

Name: Rack Pull
How to: Set the barbell in a rack at about knee height and grip it with your shins close to the bar. Stand up by driving the hips forward and squeezing the glutes, then lower it back to the pins.
Form check: Flat back from start to finish · Drive the hips forward to lock out · Lower to the pins, do not drop the bar

Name: Rear Delt Reverse Fly (Cable)
How to: Set both pulleys above head height and grab the left handle with your right hand and the right handle with your left so the cables cross in front. Pull your arms apart and back in a wide arc until they reach out to your sides. Squeeze the rear delts, then return under control.
Form check: Cross the cables in front · Sweep wide and back to your sides · Keep arms level with your shoulders

Name: Rear Delt Reverse Fly (Dumbbell)
How to: Hinge forward with a flat back holding a dumbbell in each hand below your chest. Raise the arms out to the sides until level with your shoulders, then lower them slowly.
Form check: Lead with the elbows · Stop level with the shoulders · Go light, this is a small muscle

Name: Rear Delt Reverse Fly (Machine)
How to: Sit facing the pad and grip the handles with your arms extended in front of you. Pull them out and back until your arms are level with your shoulders, then return under control.
Form check: Chest stays against the pad · Lead with the elbows, not the hands · Squeeze the shoulder blades at the back

Name: Renegade Row (Dumbbell)
How to: Set up in a push up position gripping a dumbbell in each hand with your feet wide. Row one dumbbell to your hip while keeping the hips square to the floor, then lower it and switch sides.
Form check: Hips stay square, resist the twist · Wide feet make it steadier · Use hex dumbbells so they do not roll

Name: Reverse Crunch
How to: Lie on your back with your hands by your sides and your knees bent over your hips. Curl the hips off the floor by pulling the knees toward your chest, then lower them slowly back down.
Form check: Lift the hips, do not just swing the legs · Lower slowly rather than dropping · Keep the lower back flat

Name: Reverse Curl (Barbell)
How to: Hold a barbell in front of your thighs with an overhand grip about shoulder width. Curl it up to shoulder height keeping the knuckles up, then lower under control.
Form check: Overhand grip, knuckles stay up · Elbows pinned at the sides · Much lighter than a normal curl

Name: Reverse Curl (Cable)
How to: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley and grip it at shoulder width with palms facing down. Stand tall with elbows tucked to your sides. Curl the bar up toward your shoulders until your biceps contract, then lower it slowly until your arms are straight.
Form check: Keep palms facing down · Pin elbows to your sides · Curl up without leaning back

Name: Reverse Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand and your palms facing down, arms fully extended. Keep your elbows close to your sides and curl the weights up until your biceps contract. Lower them slowly until your arms are straight, holding the palms-down grip.
Form check: Keep palms facing down · Elbows stay close to your sides

Name: Reverse Fly Single Arm (Cable)
How to: Stand side on to a cable set at chest height and take the handle in the far hand across your body. Sweep the arm out and back until level with the shoulder, then return under control.
Form check: Sweep across and back, not straight down · Stop level with the shoulder · Keep the torso still, do not twist

Name: Reverse Grip Concentration Curl
How to: Sit with your legs apart and brace the back of your upper arm against the inside of your thigh, holding the dumbbell with an overhand grip. Curl it up keeping the knuckles high, then lower slowly.
Form check: Overhand grip, knuckles stay up · Upper arm braced on the thigh · Go much lighter than a normal curl

Name: Reverse Grip Lat Pulldown (Cable)
How to: Sit with your thighs under the pads and take an underhand grip about shoulder width. Pull the bar to your upper chest keeping the elbows close to your body, then return to a full stretch.
Form check: Underhand grip about shoulder width · Elbows stay close to the ribs · Chest tall, do not lean far back

Name: Reverse Hyperextension
How to: Lie face down on a bench or hyperextension machine with your hips at the edge and your legs hanging. Raise the straight legs until they line up with your torso, then lower them under control.
Form check: Stop when the legs reach level with the torso · Squeeze the glutes at the top · Lower slowly, do not swing

Name: Reverse Lunge
How to: Stand tall and step one leg back into a long stride. Lower until the back knee is just above the floor, then push through the front heel to bring the back leg forward to standing.
Form check: Step back, not forward · Torso stays upright · Push through the front heel to return

Name: Reverse Lunge (Barbell)
How to: Set a barbell across your upper back and step one leg back into a long stride. Lower until the back knee nearly touches the floor, then drive through the front heel to stand.
Form check: Torso stays upright under the bar · Step straight back, not across · Drive through the front heel

Name: Reverse Lunge (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides. Step backward with one leg and lower your hips until both knees bend near 90 degrees and the back knee nearly touches the floor. Drive through the front heel back to standing, then alternate legs.
Form check: Step straight back · Keep weight on front heel

Name: Reverse Plank
How to: Sit with your legs straight and your hands on the floor behind your hips, fingers pointing forward. Lift the hips until your body forms a straight line from heels to shoulders and hold.
Form check: Straight line from heels to shoulders · Squeeze the glutes to hold the hips up · Keep the shoulders down away from the ears

Name: Ring Dip (Rings Turned Out)
How to: Perform ring dips and finish each press by turning the rings out so the palms face forward at the top. Hold that turnout for a moment before the next rep.
Form check: Turn the rings out at the top · Elbows stay in · Start with a short turned out hold

Name: Ring Dips
How to: Support on rings with straight arms and the rings held close to the hips. Lower under control to the bottom, then press back up while stopping the rings from drifting out.
Form check: Keep the rings pinned near the hips · Slow and controlled · Straight arms at the top

Name: Romanian Deadlift (Barbell)
How to: Stand tall holding a barbell at your thighs with your knees slightly bent. Push the hips back and lower the bar along your legs until you feel the hamstrings stretch, then drive the hips forward to stand.
Form check: Push the hips back rather than bending the knees · Bar stays in contact with the legs · Stop where the back would start to round

Name: Romanian Deadlift (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs with your knees slightly bent. Push the hips back and lower the weights down the front of your legs, then stand tall by driving the hips forward.
Form check: Weights stay close to the legs · Flat back, hips travel back · Stop at the point the hamstrings run out of stretch

Name: Rope Cable Curl
How to: Attach a rope to a low pulley and hold one end in each hand with your elbows at your sides. Curl the rope up, turning the palms slightly out at the top, then lower against the cable.
Form check: Elbows pinned at the sides · Spread the rope slightly at the top · Keep tension at the bottom, no resting

Name: Rope Straight Arm Pulldown
How to: Attach a rope to a high pulley and stand a couple feet back with a staggered stance. Hinge forward from the hips with a straight back and take the rope with arms extended overhead. Sweep your arms down to your thighs, then control back up.
Form check: Spread the rope at your thighs · Arms straight, drive from the lats

Name: Rowing Machine
How to: Strap in with your shins vertical and your arms straight. Drive with the legs first, then swing the torso back and finish by pulling the handle to your ribs, and reverse that order on the return.
Form check: Legs, then back, then arms · Return in the opposite order · Keep the chain moving level, do not yank up

Name: Running
How to: Run at a pace you can hold for the whole session, landing under your hips rather than reaching out in front. Keep the shoulders relaxed and let the arms swing forward and back, not across the body.
Form check: Land with the foot under the hips · Shoulders stay relaxed · Arms swing forward and back, not across

Name: Russian Twist (Bodyweight)
How to: Sit with the knees bent and torso leaned back, feet up or down. Rotate the torso to touch the weight or hands to each side under control.
Form check: Rotate through the trunk, not just the arms · keep the chest up and back braced · move under control, no flinging · keep the core tight throughout

Name: Russian Twist (Weighted)
How to: Sit with your knees bent and lean your torso back to about forty five degrees, holding a plate or dumbbell at your chest. Rotate the weight to one side, then the other, turning through the ribs.
Form check: Rotate through the ribs, not just the arms · Keep the chest lifted, do not slump · Raise the feet only if the back stays flat

Name: Scapular Pull Ups
How to: Hang from the bar with straight arms. Without bending the elbows, pull the shoulder blades down and together so the body rises an inch or two, then lower back to a relaxed hang.
Form check: Elbows stay straight · Move only the shoulder blades · Pause at the top of each rep

Name: Seated Cable Row - Bar Grip
How to: Sit at the cable row with your feet on the platform and a slight knee bend, gripping the straight bar. Pull it to your lower ribs by driving the elbows back, then return to a full stretch.
Form check: Torso stays upright, do not rock · Pull to the lower ribs · Let the shoulder blades open at the front

Name: Seated Cable Row - Bar Wide Grip
How to: Sit at the cable row and take a wide overhand grip on the long bar. Pull it to your upper stomach with the elbows flaring out to the sides, then return to a full stretch.
Form check: Wide grip means the elbows flare out · Pull to the upper stomach · Keep the torso still through the pull

Name: Seated Cable Row - V Grip (Cable)
How to: Sit with your feet planted and a slight knee bend, holding the V handle with both hands. Pull it to your stomach keeping the elbows close to your body, then return to a full stretch.
Form check: Elbows stay close to the ribs · Torso upright, no rocking back and forth · Full stretch at the front of each rep

Name: Seated Calf Raise
How to: Sit with the pad on the lower thighs and the balls of the feet on the block. Lower the heels to a stretch, then press up as high as possible onto the toes.
Form check: Full stretch at the bottom · press up as high as possible · pause at the top · keep the reps smooth and controlled

Name: Seated Chest Flys (Cable)
How to: Sit on a bench between two cable pulleys set at chest height with a handle in each hand. Bring the handles together in front of your chest with a soft elbow bend, then open back to a stretch.
Form check: Keep the elbow angle fixed · Bring the hands together in front of the chest · Open slowly to a stretch, do not bounce

Name: Seated Dip Machine
How to: Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles beside your hips. Press down until your arms are almost straight, squeezing the triceps, then let the handles rise back to a stretch.
Form check: Back stays flat on the pad · Press down with the triceps, do not lean forward · Stop just short of locking out

Name: Seated Incline Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Sit on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand at arm's length with elbows close to your sides. Curl the weights up while rotating your palms to face up, until your biceps contract. Lower slowly and rotate back to the start.
Form check: Keep elbows pinned to your sides · Rotate palms up as you curl · Untwist to neutral on the way down

Name: Seated Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
How to: Sit on the end of a bench with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and a slight elbow bend. Raise the arms out to the sides to shoulder height, then lower them slowly.
Form check: Sitting removes the swing, so keep the torso still · Stop at shoulder height · Lead with the elbows

Name: Seated Leg Curl (Machine)
How to: Sit with the pad on the lower calves and thighs secured. Curl the heels down and back under the seat, squeeze, then return under control.
Form check: Keep the thighs pinned under the pad · full range curl · squeeze the hamstrings · control the return

Name: Seated Overhead Press (Barbell)
How to: Sit on an upright bench with the bar at shoulder height and your grip just outside your shoulders. Press it overhead until the arms lock, then lower back to the shoulders under control.
Form check: Back stays against the pad · Ribs down, do not arch away from the bench · Lower all the way to the shoulders

Name: Seated Overhead Press (Dumbbell)
How to: Sit on a bench with back support and bring a dumbbell to each shoulder, palms facing forward. Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms extend and the weights nearly meet. Lower them under control back to shoulder height.
Form check: Press until dumbbells nearly meet · Keep your back on the pad

Name: Seated Palms Up Wrist Curl
How to: Sit on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand with your palms facing up. Rest your forearms along your thighs so the wrists hang just past your knees. Let the dumbbells roll down toward your fingers, then curl them up by flexing your wrists fully.
Form check: Roll the bells down to your fingers · Curl up, only the wrists move

Name: Seated Row (Machine)
How to: Sit with your chest against the pad and grip the handles at arms length. Pull them back until your elbows pass your torso, squeeze the shoulder blades, then return to a full stretch.
Form check: Chest stays on the pad · Pull the elbows past the torso · Let the shoulder blades open at the front

Name: Seated Shoulder Press (Machine)
How to: Sit with your back flat against the pad and the handles level with your shoulders. Press them overhead until the arms are almost straight, then lower back to shoulder height.
Form check: Set the seat so the handles start at shoulder height · Back flat on the pad · Stop just short of locking out

Name: Seated Triceps Press
How to: Sit on a bench with back support and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands, arms locked out. Keep your elbows pointing forward and lower the weight behind your head by bending the elbows. Press it back up to full extension.
Form check: Point your elbows forward, not out · Lower behind your head

Name: Seated Wrist Extension (Barbell)
How to: Sit with your forearms resting on your thighs and your wrists past the knees, holding a light barbell with an overhand grip. Raise the backs of the hands toward you, then lower slowly.
Form check: Forearms stay flat on the thighs · Move only the wrists · Very light load, the forearms fatigue fast

Name: Shoulder Press (Dumbbell)
How to: Seated or standing, start with the dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward. Press overhead until the arms extend, then lower under control to the shoulders.
Form check: Brace the core, don't arch the lower back · press slightly in, not straight out · full lockout overhead · control the weight back to the shoulders

Name: Shoulder Press (Machine Plates)
How to: Sit with your back against the pad and grip the handles at shoulder height. Press them overhead until the arms are nearly straight, then lower back under control without letting the plates drop.
Form check: Back stays flat on the pad · Press up, not forward · Lower slowly rather than letting the weight fall

Name: Shoulder Taps
How to: Set up in a push up position with your feet wide and your body straight. Lift one hand to tap the opposite shoulder, then set it down and switch, keeping the hips as still as you can.
Form check: Hips stay square, resist the rocking · Wide feet make it steadier · Tap slowly rather than rushing

Name: Shrimp Squat (Advanced)
How to: Hold the rear foot behind you and lower until the back knee touches, keeping the torso upright and the balance steady with no assistance.
Form check: Upright torso · Smooth touch and stand · No wobble at the bottom

Name: Shrimp Squat (Beginner)
How to: Hold one foot behind you with the same side hand and lower on the other leg until the back knee touches a pad. Use a light support with the free hand.
Form check: Back knee touches a pad · Free hand for balance · Torso stays upright

Name: Shrimp Squat (Intermediate)
How to: Hold the rear foot with the same side hand and lower to the back knee without any hand support. Stand back up on the working leg.
Form check: No hand support · Back knee taps the floor · Keep the chest tall

Name: Shrug (Barbell)
How to: Hold the bar in front of the thighs with straight arms. Shrug the shoulders straight up toward the ears, hold briefly, then lower under control.
Form check: Lift straight up, don't roll the shoulders · keep the arms straight · squeeze the traps at the top · control the lowering

Name: Shrug (Cable)
How to: Stand facing away from or beside a low pulley holding the handle or bar at arms length. Lift the shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, then lower them fully.
Form check: Straight up and down, do not roll the shoulders · Pause at the top · Let the shoulders drop fully at the bottom

Name: Shrug (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides with the arms straight. Lift the shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as you can, pause, then lower them fully.
Form check: Arms stay straight, this is not a pull · Straight up, no rolling · Full drop at the bottom for the stretch

Name: Shrug (Machine)
How to: Stand or sit in the machine gripping the handles with your arms straight. Lift the shoulders straight up toward your ears, hold briefly, then lower them all the way down.
Form check: Keep the arms straight throughout · Pause at the top · Lower fully rather than half repping

Name: Shrug (Smith Machine)
How to: Stand inside the Smith machine holding the bar at arms length in front of your thighs. Lift the shoulders straight up toward your ears, pause, then lower them fully.
Form check: The rails fix the path so just go straight up · Arms stay straight · Full range down before the next rep

Name: Side Bend
How to: Stand tall with your feet hip width and one hand behind your head. Bend sideways at the waist toward the free hand, then contract the opposite side to pull yourself back upright.
Form check: Bend straight sideways, do not twist or lean forward · Move slowly through the range · Same reps on both sides

Name: Side Bend (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand holding a dumbbell in one hand at your side with the other hand behind your head. Bend sideways toward the weight, then pull back up using the opposite side of your waist.
Form check: Weight on one side only · Bend straight sideways, no twisting · Do not use a weight that pulls you over

Name: Side Plank
How to: Lie on your side and prop yourself on one forearm with the elbow under the shoulder and your feet stacked. Lift the hips until your body is a straight line and hold, then switch sides.
Form check: Elbow directly under the shoulder · Hips stay lifted, no sagging · Drop the bottom knee to scale it down

Name: Single Arm Cable Crossover
How to: Set the pulley high and take the handle in one hand, stepping forward so the arm is extended out and back. Keep your chest up and pull the handle down and across your body toward the opposite hip. Squeeze the chest, then return slowly to the stretch.
Form check: Pull down across to the far hip · Stand tall, don't twist the torso

Name: Single Arm Cable Row
How to: Sit or stand facing a cable set at chest height and take the handle in one hand with the arm extended. Pull it to your ribs by driving the elbow back, then return to a full stretch.
Form check: Do not rotate the torso into the pull · Let the shoulder reach forward at the front · Elbow drives back past the ribs

Name: Single Arm Curl (Cable)
How to: Grab a single handle at the low pulley and step back so the cable stays taut. Pin your upper arm to your side and keep it still. Curl the handle up toward your shoulder by squeezing the biceps, then lower slowly to a full stretch.
Form check: Pin your upper arm to your side · Keep the cable taut at the bottom

Name: Single Arm Landmine Press (Barbell)
How to: Hold the end of a landmine barbell at your shoulder with one hand and stand square. Press it up and slightly forward until the arm locks out, then lower it back to the shoulder.
Form check: Press up and slightly forward along the bar path · Keep the ribs down and hips square · Brace so you do not lean away

Name: Single Arm Lat Pulldown
How to: Attach a single handle to a high pulley and sit with the knee pad snug against your thighs. Grip the handle with your palm facing forward and arm extended overhead. Pull it down, driving your elbow to your side, then control it back up.
Form check: Drive your elbow down to your ribs · Reach tall for a full stretch · Keep shoulders level, no twist

Name: Single Arm Lateral Raise (Cable)
How to: Stand side on to a low pulley and take the handle in the outside hand across your body. Raise the arm out to the side to shoulder height, then lower it slowly against the cable.
Form check: Stop at shoulder height · Keep the torso still, do not lean away · Resist the cable on the way down

Name: Single Arm Tricep Extension (Dumbbell)
How to: Sit or stand tall and raise a dumbbell overhead in one hand with the arm fully extended. Keep your upper arm close to your head and pointing up. Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending the elbow, then extend your arm to press it back overhead.
Form check: Keep the upper arm pointing up · Lower behind your head

Name: Single Arm Triceps Pushdown (Cable)
How to: Stand facing a high pulley with a single handle and your elbow tucked at your side. Press the handle down until the arm is straight, squeeze the triceps, then let it rise back to a bent elbow.
Form check: Elbow stays pinned at your side · Full lockout at the bottom · Do not lean into the weight to move it

Name: Single Leg Extensions
How to: Sit on a bench or chair with one leg hanging. Straighten that leg until it is fully extended, squeeze the quad at the top, then lower it under control and repeat before switching.
Form check: Full lockout at the top · Lower slowly rather than dropping · Same reps on both legs

Name: Single Leg Glute Bridge
How to: Lie on your back with feet flat and knees bent, then lift one knee toward your chest. Drive through the heel of your planted foot and extend your hip to raise your hips off the floor until your body forms a straight line. Lower under control to the floor.
Form check: Drive through your planted heel · Keep both hips level as you rise

Name: Single Leg Hip Thrust
How to: Rest your upper back on a bench with one foot flat on the floor and the other leg lifted. Drive through the planted heel to raise the hips until level, then lower under control.
Form check: Hips stay level, do not tip toward the free leg · Squeeze the glute at the top · Ribs down, no arching

Name: Single Leg Hip Thrust (Dumbbell)
How to: Rest your upper back on a bench with a dumbbell across your hips and one foot planted. Raise the hips until your body is level, squeeze, then lower under control and repeat on the other side.
Form check: Hold the dumbbell steady on the hip · Keep the hips square, no tipping · Full squeeze at the top

Name: Single Leg Press (Machine)
How to: Sit in the leg press and place one foot in the middle of the platform. Lower until the knee reaches about ninety degrees, then press back up without locking the knee hard.
Form check: Foot centered on the platform · Hips stay square on the seat · Do not slam the knee straight

Name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift (Barbell)
How to: Hold a barbell in front of your thighs and shift your weight onto one leg. Hinge forward letting the free leg travel back as a counterweight, then drive the hips forward to stand tall.
Form check: Hips stay square, do not open to the side · Free leg travels back in line with the body · Flat back throughout

Name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift (Bodyweight)
How to: Stand on one leg with a soft knee and hinge at the hips, letting the free leg travel back as the chest lowers. Return by driving the hips forward.
Form check: Hinge at the hips, not the waist · Back stays flat · Hips stay level

Name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a dumbbell in one or both hands and stand on one leg with a soft knee bend. Hinge forward lowering the weight toward the floor as the free leg lifts behind, then stand back up.
Form check: Keep the hips square to the floor · Free leg rises in line with the torso · Touch a wall or rack for balance if needed

Name: Single Leg Standing Calf Raise
How to: Stand on one foot on the edge of a step with the heel hanging off, holding something for balance. Press up onto the toes as high as you can, then lower the heel below the step.
Form check: Full stretch below the step · Rise all the way onto the toes · Hold something light for balance, do not pull on it

Name: Single Leg Standing Calf Raise (Barbell)
How to: Set a loaded barbell across your upper back and place the balls of your feet on a block or plate with heels hanging off. Rise up onto your toes as high as possible, squeezing the calves hard. Lower your heels below the block for a deep stretch.
Form check: Rise to full tip-toe · Sink the heels below the block

Name: Single Leg Standing Calf Raise (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a sturdy object for balance and place the balls of both feet on a dumbbell handle, heels on the floor. Rise onto your toes as high as you can by squeezing the calves. Lower your heels back toward the floor under control for a full stretch.
Form check: Rise as high as you can · Steady the wobbling handle

Name: Single Leg Standing Calf Raise (Machine)
How to: Set the shoulder pads and stand on the platform with one foot, the heel hanging off the edge. Press up onto the toes, pause at the top, then lower the heel for a full stretch.
Form check: Ball of the foot on the platform edge · Pause at the top rather than bouncing · Full stretch at the bottom

Name: Sissy Squat (Weighted)
How to: Grip a squat rack upright with one hand and hold a weight plate against your chest with the other, feet shoulder-width and up on your toes. Lower by driving your knees forward and leaning your torso back in a straight line. Pull with your quads to rise back up.
Form check: Drive your knees forward · Keep your body in a straight line

Name: Sit Up
How to: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet anchored, and hands behind your head. Curl your torso up off the floor toward your knees, leading with your chest. Lower back down with control until your shoulders touch.
Form check: Don't yank on your neck · Roll up through the spine · Lead with your chest

Name: Sit Up (Weighted)
How to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and hold a plate against your chest. Sit all the way up until your torso is upright, then lower back down under control.
Form check: Hold the plate close to the chest · Curl up rather than yanking with the neck · Lower slowly, do not drop back

Name: Skullcrusher (Barbell)
How to: Lie on a bench holding an EZ bar over your chest with a close grip. Bend only at the elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead, then extend back to straight arms.
Form check: Upper arms stay still, only the elbows bend · Lower to the forehead or just behind · Use an EZ bar to spare the wrists

Name: Skullcrusher (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand over your chest with palms facing each other. Bend the elbows to lower the weights beside your head, then press back to straight arms.
Form check: Upper arms stay vertical and still · Lower beside the head, not onto it · Control the descent, no dropping

Name: Sled Push
How to: Load the sled and grip the handles with your arms fully extended. Set an athletic stance with a forward body lean and a flat back. Drive the sled forward by powering through the balls of your feet, fully extending the hips and knees with every stride.
Form check: Arms long, back flat · Push through the balls of the feet · Fully extend hips and knees

Name: Snatch
How to: From a wide grip, pull the bar explosively from the floor, extend the hips and pull under to catch it overhead in a full squat, then stand to lockout.
Form check: Wide grip, bar close and over the mid-foot · explode through the hips · pull under fast to a locked-out catch · stay tight and stand tall to finish

Name: Snowboarding
How to: Ride at a pace and terrain that keeps you working continuously, staying low with the knees bent and the weight centered over the board. Link turns smoothly rather than skidding to a stop.
Form check: Stay low with the knees bent · Weight centered over the board · Link turns rather than stopping and starting

Name: Spider Curl (Barbell)
How to: Lie chest down on an incline bench with your arms hanging straight below you holding an EZ bar. Curl it up toward your shoulders without moving the upper arms, then lower to straight.
Form check: Chest stays on the bench · Upper arms hang still throughout · Lower all the way to straight arms

Name: Spider Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Lie face down on an incline bench with your chest supported and shoulders near the top. Let your arms hang straight down holding a dumbbell in each hand. Curl the weights up toward your shoulders, then lower them under control to a full stretch.
Form check: Lie chest-down on the bench · Let arms hang straight down

Name: Spiderman
How to: Set up in a push up position with your body straight. Drive one knee up toward the same side elbow, hold briefly, then return it and switch sides.
Form check: Knee travels to the outside of the elbow · Hips stay low and level · Move under control, not at speed

Name: Spinning
How to: Ride a stationary bike through changes of pace and resistance, staying seated or standing as the session calls for. Keep the pedal stroke smooth and the upper body relaxed.
Form check: Set the saddle to hip height before starting · Smooth circular pedal stroke · Keep the shoulders relaxed, not hunched

Name: Split Jerk
How to: Rack the bar across your front delts, feet under your hips. Dip straight down by bending the knees, then drive up explosively and punch the bar overhead. As it rises, split one foot forward and one back into a lunge and lock the arms, then recover the feet to standing.
Form check: Dip straight down, torso tall · Drive through legs, not arms · Split feet front and back · Catch with arms locked out

Name: Split Squat (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and set your feet in a long split stance. Lower straight down until the back knee is just above the floor, then drive through the front heel to stand.
Form check: Feet stay in place the whole set · Lower straight down, not forward · Front shin close to vertical

Name: Sprints
How to: Run at close to maximum effort for a short distance or time, then walk or jog until you have recovered. Drive the knees and pump the arms hard through each sprint.
Form check: Build up to full speed rather than exploding cold · Recover fully between efforts · Stop the session when the speed drops off

Name: Squat (Assisted)
How to: Hold a doorframe, pole or suspension strap and sit back into a squat. Use the hands for balance and only as much pull as you need to reach depth.
Form check: Use the hands for balance · Sit back and down · Heels stay flat

Name: Squat (Assisted, Deep)
How to: Using the same light support, lower all the way until the hamstrings meet the calves. Hold the bottom briefly, then stand back up.
Form check: Go to full depth · Pause at the bottom · Keep the heels down

Name: Squat (Band)
How to: Stand on the band with your feet shoulder width and bring the top of the loop over your shoulders. Squat down until the thighs are at least parallel, then stand up against the band.
Form check: Keep the band settled on the shoulders · Knees track over the toes · Chest stays tall through the rep

Name: Squat (Barbell)
How to: Set the bar just below shoulder height, step under it and rest it across your upper back. Drive through your legs to unrack, step back to a shoulder-width stance with toes slightly out. Sit the hips back and bend the knees until the hamstrings meet the calves, then drive up through the mid-foot to standing.
Form check: Head up, back flat throughout · brace before you descend · inhale down, exhale up · push the floor away through heel and mid-foot · knees track over the toes

Name: Squat (Bodyweight)
How to: Stand with the feet about shoulder width and the toes turned slightly out. Sit back and down until the thighs pass parallel, then drive through the whole foot to stand.
Form check: Knees track over the toes · Thighs past parallel · Chest stays up

Name: Squat (Deep)
How to: Squat all the way to the bottom so the hamstrings rest on the calves and hold there comfortably. Stand back up without letting the heels lift.
Form check: Full depth, heels down · Hold the bottom position · Keep the spine long

Name: Squat (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides or one at your chest, feet about shoulder width. Squat down until your thighs are at least parallel, then drive through the floor to stand.
Form check: Chest stays tall, do not fold forward · Knees track over the toes · Heels stay down the whole way

Name: Squat (Machine)
How to: Set the shoulder pads and place your feet on the platform about shoulder width. Lower until your thighs are at least parallel, then press back up through the whole foot.
Form check: Back stays flat against the pad · Whole foot stays on the platform · Do not lock the knees hard at the top

Name: Squat (Smith Machine)
How to: Set the bar across your upper back in the Smith machine with your feet slightly forward. Lower until your thighs are at least parallel, then drive back up and re-engage the hooks at the end.
Form check: Feet slightly forward of the bar · Rails fix the path so drive straight up · Set the safeties before you start

Name: Squat (Suspension)
How to: Hold the handles and stand with your feet shoulder width and the straps taut. Sit back into a squat using the straps for balance, then drive through the heels to stand.
Form check: Use the straps for balance, not to pull yourself up · Chest stays tall · Sit the hips back as you descend

Name: Squat Row
How to: Hold the suspension handles or a band and sink into a squat with your arms extended. Stand up while pulling the handles to your ribs, then squat back down as the arms extend.
Form check: Squat and row flow as one movement · Elbows drive back at the top · Chest stays tall in the squat

Name: Stair Machine (Floors)
How to: Step onto the machine and climb at a steady pace, standing tall rather than leaning on the rails. Place the whole foot on each step and let the legs do the work.
Form check: Stand tall, do not hang off the handles · Whole foot on each step · Keep a pace you can hold for the session

Name: Stair Machine (Steps)
How to: Climb at a steady step rate, standing upright with a light touch on the rails for balance only. Drive through the whole foot on each step rather than the toes alone.
Form check: Light touch on the rails, no leaning · Full foot on each step · Hold a steady step rate

Name: Standing Cable Glute Kickbacks
How to: Attach an ankle strap to a low pulley and face the machine holding on for balance. Drive the strapped leg back and up by squeezing the glute, then return under control.
Form check: Push with the glute, do not arch the back · Torso stays upright · Return slowly rather than letting it snap back

Name: Standing Calf Raise
How to: Set a loaded barbell across your upper back inside a squat rack and step out. Rise up onto the balls of your feet as high as you can, squeezing the calves. Rock back onto your heels and lift your toes, then rock forward onto your toes again.
Form check: Rise onto your toes, then rock back · Lift your toes at the heel end · Rock smoothly, no bouncing

Name: Standing Calf Raise (Barbell)
How to: Set a loaded barbell across your upper back and place the balls of your feet on a block or plate with heels hanging off. Rise up onto your toes as high as possible, squeezing the calves hard. Lower your heels below the block for a deep stretch.
Form check: Rise to full tip-toe · Sink the heels below the block

Name: Standing Calf Raise (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a sturdy object for balance and place the balls of both feet on a dumbbell handle, heels on the floor. Rise onto your toes as high as you can by squeezing the calves. Lower your heels back toward the floor under control for a full stretch.
Form check: Rise as high as you can · Steady the wobbling handle

Name: Standing Calf Raise (Machine)
How to: Set the shoulder pads and stand with the balls of your feet on the platform edge. Press up onto the toes as high as you can, pause, then lower the heels below the platform.
Form check: Balls of the feet on the edge · Full stretch at the bottom · Pause at the top instead of bouncing

Name: Standing Calf Raise (Smith)
How to: Set the bar across your upper back in the Smith machine and stand with the balls of your feet on a block. Press up onto the toes, pause, then lower the heels for a full stretch.
Form check: Use a block so the heels can drop below · Pause at the top · Rise all the way onto the toes

Name: Standing Leg Curls
How to: Stand tall holding something for balance and shift your weight onto one leg. Curl the other heel toward your glute as far as it goes, then lower it under control.
Form check: Keep the thigh still, only the knee bends · Stand tall, do not lean forward · Curl as far as the heel will travel

Name: Standing Military Press (Barbell)
How to: Hold the bar at the front of the shoulders, feet hip-width, glutes and abs braced. Press the bar overhead, moving the head back slightly to clear it, then push through to a locked-out finish over the mid-foot.
Form check: Squeeze the glutes and abs, don't lean back · bar travels in a straight line over the mid-foot · full lockout with the biceps by the ears · keep the ribs down

Name: Step Up
How to: Place one whole foot on a box at about knee height. Drive through that heel to stand up on the box without pushing off the back foot, then lower back down under control.
Form check: Whole foot on the box · Drive through the top heel · Lower slowly rather than dropping down

Name: Sternum Pull up (Gironda)
How to: Hang from the bar and pull while leaning your head back and arching the upper back. Keep pulling until your sternum touches the bar and your body finishes close to horizontal, then lower under control.
Form check: Lean the head back as you pull · Sternum meets the bar, not the chin · Lower slowly, this range is demanding

Name: Straight Arm Lat Pulldown (Cable)
How to: Grab a wide bar on a high pulley with an overhand grip wider than shoulder width and step back about two feet. Hinge your torso forward about 30 degrees with arms extended toward the pulley. Sweep the bar down to your thighs in an arc, then return under control.
Form check: Sweep the bar down in an arc · Move only at the shoulders

Name: Straight Leg Deadlift
How to: Stand with your feet hip width and your knees nearly locked. Hinge at the hips to lower your hands toward the floor until the hamstrings stop you, then drive the hips forward to stand.
Form check: Knees stay nearly straight · Stop where the back would start to round · Push the hips back, do not just bend over

Name: Stretching
How to: Move into each position until you feel a mild stretch, then hold it while you breathe steadily. Ease off if the sensation turns sharp and give both sides the same time.
Form check: Mild stretch, never sharp pain · Breathe rather than holding your breath · Give both sides equal time

Name: Sumo Deadlift
How to: Stand with a wide stance and your toes turned out, hands inside your knees. Push the knees out, keep the chest up and drive through the floor to stand tall, then lower under control.
Form check: Wide stance, hands inside the knees · Push the knees out over the toes · Chest up, hips and shoulders rise together

Name: Sumo Squat
How to: Stand with your feet much wider than your shoulders and your toes turned out. Squat straight down between your heels keeping the chest tall, then drive through the floor to stand.
Form check: Knees track out over the toes · Drop straight down, not back · Chest stays tall throughout

Name: Sumo Squat (Barbell)
How to: Set a barbell across your upper back and take a wide stance with your toes turned out. Squat straight down until the thighs pass parallel, then drive up through the whole foot.
Form check: Knees push out in line with the toes · Torso stays upright · Whole foot stays planted

Name: Sumo Squat (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a single dumbbell with both hands hanging between your legs and take a wide stance with toes out. Squat straight down until the thighs pass parallel, then stand and squeeze the glutes.
Form check: Let the dumbbell travel straight down between the legs · Knees push out · Chest stays tall

Name: Sumo Squat (Kettlebell)
How to: Hold a kettlebell by the handle with both hands hanging in front of you and take a wide stance with toes out. Squat down between your heels, then drive up to standing.
Form check: Bell travels straight down between the legs · Knees track over the toes · Keep the back flat and chest up

Name: Superman
How to: Lie face down with your arms extended overhead. Lift your arms, chest and legs off the floor at the same time, hold briefly, then lower everything back down under control.
Form check: Lift arms and legs together · Look at the floor, do not crank the neck up · Hold briefly rather than bouncing

Name: Swimming
How to: Swim continuous lengths at a pace you can hold, breathing on a regular rhythm. Keep the body long and flat in the water and let the legs stay near the surface.
Form check: Keep the body long and flat · Breathe on a regular rhythm · Steady pace rather than sprint and rest

Name: T Bar Row
How to: Straddle the bar and grip the handles with a flat back and your torso hinged forward. Row the weight to your chest by driving the elbows back, then lower it to a full stretch.
Form check: Flat back, hinged at the hips · Pull to the chest, elbows drive back · Let the shoulder blades open at the bottom

Name: Thruster (Barbell)
How to: Hold the bar in a front rack across your shoulders and squat down to at least parallel. Drive up out of the squat and use that momentum to press the bar overhead in one motion.
Form check: Squat and press are one movement · Elbows stay up in the rack position · Finish with the bar over the mid foot

Name: Thruster (Kettlebell)
How to: Hold two kettlebells racked at your shoulders, feet shoulder-width. Squat down until your thighs are parallel, then drive up through the legs and press both bells overhead as you stand. Lower back to the shoulders and descend again.
Form check: Hit parallel in the squat · Drive up through the legs · Press as you stand · Lock out overhead

Name: Toe Touch
How to: Lie on your back with your legs raised straight toward the ceiling and your arms reaching up. Curl the shoulders off the floor to reach for your toes, then lower back under control.
Form check: Reach with the shoulders, not just the hands · Keep the legs vertical and still · Lower back stays flat

Name: Toes to Bar
How to: Hang from the bar with the shoulders active. Swing into a slight arch, then drive the legs up until your toes touch the bar, and control the way back down into the next rep.
Form check: Toes actually touch the bar · Keep the shoulders active in the hang · Learn hanging leg raises first

Name: Torso Rotation
How to: Sit or stand with the pad or handle against your torso and your hips locked in place. Rotate your upper body to one side against the resistance, then return under control.
Form check: Rotate through the ribs, keep the hips still · Move slowly in both directions · Same reps on both sides

Name: Treadmill
How to: Set a pace and incline you can hold and run or walk in the middle of the belt. Stand tall and let the arms swing naturally rather than holding the rails.
Form check: Do not hold the handrails · Stay in the middle of the belt · Land with the foot under the hips

Name: Triceps Dip
How to: Support yourself on parallel bars with straight arms and your torso close to upright. Lower until the elbows reach about ninety degrees, then press back to straight arms.
Form check: Stay upright to keep it on the triceps · Elbows track back, not out · Full lockout at the top

Name: Triceps Dip (Assisted)
How to: Kneel on the assist pad or loop a band under your knees on the parallel bars and stay upright. Lower until the elbows reach ninety degrees, then press back to straight arms.
Form check: Use the least assistance you can manage · Stay upright through the rep · Elbows stay close to the body

Name: Triceps Dip (Weighted)
How to: Add load with a dip belt or vest and support yourself upright on the parallel bars. Lower until the elbows reach ninety degrees, then press back to a full lockout.
Form check: Record the added load only · Stay upright to keep it on the triceps · Full range before adding more weight
Equipment: Dip bars; weight belt or vest

Name: Triceps Extension (Barbell)
How to: Lie back on an incline bench set between 45 and 75 degrees, holding a barbell with an overhand grip just inside shoulder width. Extend your arms to bring the bar overhead with elbows in. Lower the bar toward the top of your head by bending the elbows, then extend back up.
Form check: Set the bench 45 to 75 degrees · Lower the bar to the top of your head

Name: Triceps Extension (Cable)
How to: Lie on a flat bench at the end of a low pulley and hold the straight bar with a narrow overhand grip. Start with your arms extended and the bar over your face. Bend your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead, then extend to press it back up.
Form check: Keep elbows tucked and still · Lower the bar toward your forehead

Name: Triceps Extension (Dumbbell)
How to: Stand with feet shoulder width and hold one dumbbell overhead with both hands, arms extended. Keep your elbows in and pointing up as you lower the weight behind your head. Press back up to full lockout overhead.
Form check: Keep your elbows pointing up · Lower behind your head

Name: Triceps Extension (Machine)
How to: Adjust the seat and set your upper arms against the pads, grasping the handles. Extend your elbows to push the handles down until your arms are straight. Return under control until your elbows are bent, keeping your upper arms on the pads.
Form check: Keep upper arms on the pads · Push down to straight arms

Name: Triceps Extension (Suspension)
How to: Hold the handles and lean forward with your body straight and your hands in front of your forehead. Straighten the arms to press yourself back up, then bend the elbows to lower under control.
Form check: Upper arms stay high and still · Body stays in one straight line · Walk the feet back to make it easier

Name: Triceps Kickback (Cable)
How to: Hinge forward holding a low cable handle with your upper arm pinned against your side. Straighten the arm behind you, squeeze the triceps, then return to a bent elbow.
Form check: Upper arm stays pinned and still · Full straighten at the back · Do not swing the torso to finish the rep

Name: Triceps Kickback (Dumbbell)
How to: Hinge forward with a flat back holding a dumbbell with your upper arm against your side. Extend the arm straight back until it locks, squeeze, then lower to a bent elbow.
Form check: Upper arm stays parallel to the floor · Only the elbow moves · Go light, this is a short range movement

Name: Triceps Pressdown
How to: Stand facing a high pulley holding a bar or rope with your elbows tucked at your sides. Press down until the arms are straight, squeeze, then let the handle rise back to a bent elbow.
Form check: Elbows pinned at the sides · Full lockout at the bottom · Do not lean over the bar to press it down

Name: Triceps Pushdown
How to: Stand at a high pulley with the elbows pinned to the sides. Extend the arms fully down, then return under control without letting the elbows drift.
Form check: Elbows stay pinned to the sides · full extension at the bottom · don't lean over the bar to push it · control the return

Name: Triceps Rope Pushdown
How to: Attach a rope to a high pulley and grip it with palms facing each other. Keep your upper arms pinned to your sides and lean the torso slightly forward. Push the rope down by extending your elbows and spread the ends apart at the bottom, then let it rise to chest height.
Form check: Pin upper arms to sides · Spread rope at the bottom

Name: Upright Row (Barbell)
How to: Grip a barbell with an overhand grip slightly narrower than shoulder width, arms hanging so the bar rests on your thighs and your back straight. Pull the bar straight up along your body toward your collarbone, leading with your elbows. Lower it under control.
Form check: Lead with your elbows · Pull to your collarbone, no swing

Name: Upright Row (Cable)
How to: Stand facing a low pulley holding a straight bar with an overhand grip at about shoulder width. Pull it up along your body to chest height, leading with the elbows, then lower under control.
Form check: Lead with the elbows · Stop at chest height, not the chin · Use a wider grip if the shoulders pinch

Name: Upright Row (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold the dumbbells in front of the thighs. Pull them straight up along the body by leading with the elbows to about chest height, then lower under control.
Form check: Lead with the elbows, keep the weights close · don't pull above chest height · control the descent · stop if the shoulders pinch

Name: V Up
How to: Lie flat with your arms overhead and your legs straight. Lift the arms and legs at the same time so they meet above your hips in a V, then lower everything back under control.
Form check: Arms and legs rise together · Reach for the toes, do not just sit up · Bend the knees to scale it down

Name: V-Sit Hold
How to: From an L-sit, compress the hips and lift the straight legs above horizontal into a V shape. Lean the shoulders slightly back to balance the weight of the legs.
Form check: Legs above horizontal · Lean the shoulders back to balance · Arms stay locked

Name: Walking
How to: Walk at a brisk pace you can hold for the session, standing tall with the shoulders relaxed. Let the arms swing naturally and roll through the whole foot with each step.
Form check: Stand tall with the shoulders relaxed · Roll through the whole foot · Keep the pace brisk enough to breathe harder

Name: Walking Lunge
How to: Step forward into a long stride and lower until the back knee is just above the floor. Drive through the front heel to stand and bring the back leg through into the next stride.
Form check: Long stride, torso stays upright · Back knee hovers, does not bang down · Keep walking rather than resetting each rep
