Name: Walking Lunge (Dumbbell)
How to: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides and step forward into a long stride. Lower until the back knee nearly touches, then drive through the front heel into the next stride.
Form check: Torso stays upright under the load · Long stride each rep · Drive through the front heel to move forward

Name: Wall Ball
How to: Hold a medicine ball at your chest and squat to at least parallel facing a wall. Drive up out of the squat and throw the ball at the target, then catch it and absorb straight into the next squat.
Form check: Squat to at least parallel every rep · Drive with the legs, not the arms · Catch and absorb into the next squat

Name: Wall Sit
How to: Lean your back flat against a wall and walk your feet out until your knees are bent to ninety degrees. Hold that position with the thighs parallel to the floor and breathe steadily.
Form check: Thighs parallel, knees at ninety degrees · Whole back stays flat on the wall · Do not rest the hands on the thighs

Name: Warm Up
How to: Spend five to ten minutes raising the heart rate and moving each joint through its range. Finish with a few light sets of the first exercise you plan to do.
Form check: Raise the heart rate first · Move the joints you are about to load · Finish with light sets of the first lift

Name: Wide Pull Up
How to: Take an overhand grip wider than shoulder width. Pull the chest toward the bar while keeping the shoulders pulled down, then lower to straight arms.
Form check: Hands wider than the shoulders · Lead with the chest · Do not shorten the range

Name: Wrist Roller
How to: Stand tall gripping a loaded wrist roller with both hands, palms down. Raise your arms straight in front until they are parallel to the floor. Wind the weight up by rolling the bar hand over hand, then slowly reverse the roll to lower it back down.
Form check: Hold arms out parallel to floor · Wind hand over hand · Unwind slowly to lower

Name: Yoga
How to: Move through a sequence of postures, holding each while you breathe steadily and keeping the transitions controlled. Work to your own range rather than forcing any position.
Form check: Breathe steadily through every hold · Work to your own range, do not force it · Keep the transitions slow and controlled

Name: Zercher Squat
How to: Hold a barbell in the crooks of your elbows against your body and stand with your feet shoulder width. Squat down keeping the chest tall and elbows inside the knees, then drive up to stand.
Form check: Bar sits in the crook of the elbows · Chest stays tall, do not fold forward · Use a pad or sleeves, the bar digs in

Name: Zottman Curl (Dumbbell)
How to: Curl a dumbbell in each hand up with the palms facing up. At the top rotate the palms to face down, then lower slowly in that overhand position and rotate back at the bottom.
Form check: Rotate at the top, lower with the palms down · Lower slower than you lift · Go light, the lowering half is the hard part

Name: Romanian Deadlift (Bodyweight)
How to: Stand tall with a slight bend in the knees. Brace your core, push your hips back and hinge your torso forward until you feel tension in the hamstrings. Squeeze the glutes and drive the hips forward to return to standing.
Form check: Hips move back, not down · Keep a neutral spine · Knees stay softly bent · Feel the stretch in the hamstrings, not the lower back

Name: Nordic Hamstring Curl (Banded, Eccentric)
How to: Kneel with your feet securely anchored and a resistance band assisting your torso. Keep your hips extended and slowly lower your body toward the floor. Catch yourself with your hands at the bottom and push back to the start instead of curling yourself up.
Form check: Straight line from knees to shoulders · Keep hips extended · Lower slowly under control · Use the hands to return, not the hamstrings

Name: Nordic Hamstring Curl (Banded)
How to: Kneel with your feet securely anchored and a resistance band assisting your torso. Keeping your hips extended, lower under control, then contract your hamstrings to pull yourself back to the starting position with assistance from the band.
Form check: Straight line from knees to shoulders · Do not pike at the hips · Control the descent · Use the band only as much as needed
